Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 50, verse 1–5 (part 1 of 2):

Tafsir of Surah Qaf

It is Meccan.

This surah is, according to the correct view, the beginning of the detailed portion of the Qur'an (al-Mufassal, the final division of the Qur'an into sections). It is also said that it begins with al-Hujurat. As for what the common people say, that it is from ('Amma), there is no basis for it, and none of the scholars whose views are considered reliable (al-mu'tabarin) has said it, to our knowledge. The evidence that this surah is the beginning of al-Mufassal is what Abu Dawud related in his Sunan, in the chapter "Dividing the Qur'an into Portions" (tahzib al-Qur'an), where he said:

Musaddad related to us: Qurran ibn Tammam related to us (ḥ). And 'Abdullah ibn Sa'id Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj related to us: Abu Khalid Sulayman ibn Hayyan related to us—and this is his wording—from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'la, from 'Uthman ibn 'Abdullah ibn Aws, from his grandfather—'Abdullah ibn Sa'id said: Aws ibn Hudhayfa related it to me—then they both agreed. He said: "We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as part of the delegation of Thaqif." He said: "The Ahlaf stayed with al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ housed Banu Malik in a tent of his." Musaddad said: "And among the delegation of Thaqif that came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was..." He said: "The Messenger of Allah [ﷺ] used to come to us every night after 'Isha, speaking to us"—Abu Sa'id said: "standing on his feet, so that he shifted his weight between his feet from the length of standing"—"and most of what he related to us was what he had encountered from his people, Quraysh. Then he would say: 'It is not equal (la sawa'). We were weak and humiliated'"—Musaddad said: "in Makkah"—"and when we went out to Madinah, the rounds of war were between us and them: we were given victory over them, and they were given victory over us. Then one night he was late for the time he used to come to us, so we said: 'You have been late with us tonight!' He said: 'My portion (hizb) of the Qur'an came upon me, and I disliked to come until I had completed it.'" Aws said: "I asked the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'How do you divide the Qur'an into portions?' They said: 'Three, five, seven, nine, eleven, thirteen, and the Mufassal alone.'"

Ibn Majah related it from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba, from Abu Khalid al-Ahmar, with the same chain. Imam Ahmad related it from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, that is Ibn Ya'la al-Ta'ifi, with it.

Having established this, if you count forty-eight surahs, the one that follows them is Surah Qaf. Its explanation: three: al-Baqarah, Ali 'Imran, and al-Nisa'. Five: al-Ma'idah, al-An'am, al-A'raf, al-Anfal, and Bara'ah. Seven: Yunus, Hud, Yusuf, al-Ra'd, Ibrahim, al-Hijr, and al-Nahl. Nine: Subhan, al-Kahf, Maryam, Ta-Ha, al-Anbiya', al-Hajj, al-Mu'minun, al-Nur, and al-Furqan. Eleven: al-Shu'ara', al-Naml, al-Qasas, al-'Ankabut, al-Rum, Luqman, al-Sajdah, al-Ahzab, Saba', Fatir, and Ya-Sin. Thirteen: al-Saffat, Sad, al-Zumar, Ghafir, Ha-Mim al-Sajdah, Ha-Mim 'Asaq, al-Zukhruf, al-Dukhan, al-Jathiyah, al-Ahqaf, Muhammad (al-Qital), al-Fath, and al-Hujurat. Then after that is al-Mufassal, as the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, stated. Thus it is established that its beginning is Surah Qaf, which is what we have stated, and to Allah belong all praise and favour.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us: Malik related to us, from Damrah ibn Sa'id, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abdullah, that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab asked Abu Waqid al-Laythi: "What did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite at the 'Eid?" He said: "Qaf, and Iqtarabat."

Muslim and the four Sunan compilers related it from the hadith of Malik, with it. In a narration of Muslim from Fulayh, from Damrah, from 'Ubayd Allah, from Abu Waqid, he said: "'Umar asked me," and he mentioned it.

Another hadith: Ahmad said: Ya'qub related to us, my father related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who related to me 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr ibn 'Amr ibn Hazm, from Yahya ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'd ibn Zurarah, from Umm Hisham bint Harithah, who said: "Our oven and the oven of the Prophet ﷺ were one for two years, or a year and some of a year. I did not learn Qaf, wal-Qur'an al-Majid except from the tongue of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; he used to recite it every Friday on the pulpit when he addressed the people."

Muslim related it from the hadith of Ibn Ishaq, with it.

Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, Shu'bah related to us, from Khubayb, from 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Ma'n, from the daughter of al-Harith ibn al-Nu'man, who said: "I did not memorise Qaf except from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who would deliver the sermon with it every Friday." She said: "And our oven and the oven of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were one."

Muslim, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah related it likewise from the hadith of Shu'bah, with it.

The purpose is that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite this surah at the great gatherings, such as the 'Eids and the Friday prayers, because it includes the origination of creation, the resurrection, the rising, the return, the reckoning, Paradise and Hell, reward and punishment, and encouragement and warning.

* *

﴿Qaf﴾: a letter from the letters of the alphabet mentioned at the beginnings of surahs, like His saying: (Sad, Nun, Alif-Lam-Mim, Ha-Mim, Ta-Sin) and similar to that. This was said by Mujahid and others. We have already discussed these letters at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah, with what suffices without repetition.

It has been related from some of the early generation (salaf) that they said "Qaf" is a mountain encircling the entire earth, called Mount Qaf. It seems that this—and Allah knows best—is among the fabrications of the Israelites which some people took from them, because they saw the permissibility of narrating from them about things that are neither confirmed nor denied. In my view, this and similar things are fabrications of some of their heretics, by which they confuse people about the matter of their religion, just as hadiths were forged about the Prophet ﷺ in this Ummah—despite the high standing of its scholars, memorisers and imams—and how much more so with the nation of the Israelites, given the long span of time, the scarcity of critical memorisers among them, their drinking of wine, their scholars' distortion of words from their places, and their alteration of the Books of Allah and His verses! The Lawgiver only permitted narration from them in His saying: "Narrate from the Children of Israel, and there is no harm," regarding what reason may allow. As for what reason rejects and what is judged to be false, and whose falsehood is strongly suspected, this is not of that category—and Allah knows best.

Many of the early exegetes, and likewise a great many of the later ones, have greatly relied on relating from the books of the People of the Book in the interpretation of the Glorious Qur'an, though they have no need of their reports—and to Allah belong all praise and favour. Indeed, the Imam Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim al-Razi, may Allah have mercy on him, cited here a strange report with an unsound chain from Ibn 'Abbas, saying:

"My father related to me, saying: I was told from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Makhzumi: Layth ibn Abi Sulaym related to us, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Allah created, beyond this earth, a encompassing sea. Then He created, beyond that, a mountain called Qaf, upon which the lowest heaven is raised. Then Allah created, beyond that mountain, an earth like this earth, seven times over. Then He created, beyond that, a sea encompassing it. Then He created, beyond that, a mountain called Qaf, upon which the second heaven is raised,' until he counted seven earths, seven seas, seven mountains, and seven heavens." He said: "That is His saying: ﴿And the sea, after it, is extended by seven seas﴾ [Luqman: 27]."

The chain of this report has a break (inqita'). What Ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying ﴿Qaf﴾ is that he said: "It is one of the names of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

What is established from Mujahid is that it is a letter of the alphabet, like His saying: (Sad, Nun, Ha-Mim, Ta-Sin, Alif-Lam-Mim) and similar. This renders the preceding report from Ibn 'Abbas far-fetched.

It has also been said: the meaning is "Qada al-amr wallahi" (the matter has been decided, by Allah), and that His saying ﴿Qaf﴾ indicates what is omitted from the rest of the phrase, like the poet's line: "I said to her: 'Stop!' so she said: 'Qaf!'..."

There is scrutiny in this interpretation, for omission in speech only occurs when a clear indication points to it, and from where is this understood from the mention of this letter?

* *

His saying ﴿and the Glorious Qur'an﴾ means: the Noble, the Great, which falsehood cannot approach from before it or from behind it, a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy.

They differed concerning what the answer to the oath is. Ibn Jarir related from some grammarians that it is His saying: ﴿We already know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a preserved Book.﴾

There is scrutiny in this, rather the answer is the content of the speech after the oath, which is the affirmation of prophethood and the affirmation of the return, and their establishment and confirmation, even if the oath is not explicitly stated. This is common in the oaths of the Qur'an, as was mentioned earlier in His saying: ﴿Sad, by the Qur'an containing the reminder. But those who disbelieve are in arrogance and opposition﴾ [Sad: 1, 2]. Likewise He said here: ﴿Qaf, by the Glorious Qur'an. Rather, they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves, and the disbelievers say, "This is a strange thing."﴾ That is: they marvelled at the sending of a messenger to them from among mankind, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Is it a wonder for the people that We revealed to a man from among them: "Warn the people"?﴾ [Yunus: 2]. That is: this is not strange, for Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among mankind.

Then He said, reporting about them in their wonder also at the Return and their deeming its occurrence unlikely: ﴿When we die and become dust—that is a far return.﴾ That is, they say: "When we die and decay, and our joints are scattered, and we become dust, how is it possible to return after that to this structure and composition?" ﴿That is a far return﴾: that is, far from occurring. The meaning of this is that they believe it impossible and not feasible.

Allah, Exalted, replied to them: ﴿We already know what the earth diminishes of them﴾: that is, what it consumes of their bodies in decay. We know that, and nothing is hidden from Us: where the bodies were scattered, where they went, and to where they arrived. ﴿And with Us is a preserved Book﴾: that is, one that preserves that. So His knowledge is comprehensive, and the Book also contains all things, precisely recorded.

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying ﴿We already know what the earth diminishes of them﴾: that is, what it eats of their flesh and skins, and their bones and hair. Likewise said Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and others.

Then Allah, exalted is He, explained the cause of their disbelief, their obstinacy, and their deeming unlikely what is not unlikely at all, so He said: ﴿Nay, they denied the truth when it came to them, so they are in a confused state.﴾ That is, this is the condition of everyone who departs from the truth; whatever such a person says afterward is false. "Marij" means what is varied, disordered, confused, and containing objectionable elements within it, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, you are in a contradictory saying. Turned away from it is whoever is turned away.﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 8, 9].

This was said by Mujahid and others. We have already discussed these letters at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah, with what suffices without repetition.

It has been related from some of the early generation (salaf) that they said "Qaf" is a mountain encircling the entire earth, called Mount Qaf. It seems that this—and Allah knows best—is among the fabrications of the Israelites which some people took from them, because they saw the permissibility of narrating from them about things that are neither confirmed nor denied. In my view, this and similar things are fabrications of some of their heretics, by which they confuse people about the matter of their religion, just as hadiths were forged about the Prophet ﷺ in this Ummah—despite the high standing of its scholars, memorisers and imams—and how much more so with the nation of the Israelites, given the long span of time, the scarcity of critical memorisers among them, their drinking of wine, their scholars' distortion of words from their places, and their alteration of the Books of Allah and His verses! The Lawgiver only permitted narration from them in His saying: "Narrate from the Children of Israel, and there is no harm," regarding what reason may allow. As for what reason rejects and what is judged to be false, and whose falsehood is strongly suspected, this is not of that category—and Allah knows best.

Many of the early exegetes, and likewise a great many of the later ones, have greatly relied on relating from the books of the People of the Book in the interpretation of the Glorious Qur'an, though they have no need of their reports—and to Allah belong all praise and favour. Indeed, the Imam Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim al-Razi, may Allah have mercy on him, cited here a strange report with an unsound chain from Ibn 'Abbas, saying:

"My father related to me, saying: I was told from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Makhzumi: Layth ibn Abi Sulaym related to us, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Allah created, beyond this earth, a encompassing sea. Then He created, beyond that, a mountain called Qaf, upon which the lowest heaven is raised. Then Allah created, beyond that mountain, an earth like this earth, seven times over. Then He created, beyond that, a sea encompassing it. Then He created, beyond that, a mountain called Qaf, upon which the second heaven is raised,' until he counted seven earths, seven seas, seven mountains, and seven heavens." He said: "That is His saying: ﴿And the sea, after it, is extended by seven seas﴾ [Luqman: 27]."

The chain of this report has a break (inqita'). What Ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying ﴿Qaf﴾ is that he said: "It is one of the names of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

What is established from Mujahid is that it is a letter of the alphabet, like His saying: (Sad, Nun, Ha-Mim, Ta-Sin, Alif-Lam-Mim) and similar. This renders the preceding report from Ibn 'Abbas far-fetched.

It has also been said: the meaning is "Qada al-amr wallahi" (the matter has been decided, by Allah), and that His saying ﴿Qaf﴾ indicates what is omitted from the rest of the phrase, like the poet's line: "I said to her: 'Stop!' so she said: 'Qaf!'..."

There is scrutiny in this interpretation, for omission in speech only occurs when a clear indication points to it, and from where is this understood from the mention of this letter?

* *

His saying ﴿and the Glorious Qur'an﴾ means: the Noble, the Great, which falsehood cannot approach from before it or from behind it, a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy.

They differed concerning what the answer to the oath is. Ibn Jarir related from some grammarians that it is His saying: ﴿We already know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a preserved Book.﴾

There is scrutiny in this, rather the answer is the content of the speech after the oath, which is the affirmation of prophethood and the affirmation of the return, and their establishment and confirmation, even if the oath is not explicitly stated. This is common in the oaths of the Qur'an, as was mentioned earlier in His saying: ﴿Sad, by the Qur'an containing the reminder. But those who disbelieve are in arrogance and opposition﴾ [Sad: 1, 2]. Likewise He said here: ﴿Qaf, by the Glorious Qur'an. Rather, they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves, and the disbelievers say, "This is a strange thing."﴾ That is: they marvelled at the sending of a messenger to them from among mankind, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Is it a wonder for the people that We revealed to a man from among them: "Warn the people"?﴾ [Yunus: 2]. That is: this is not strange, for Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among mankind.

Then He said, reporting about them in their wonder also at the Return and their deeming its occurrence unlikely: ﴿When we die and become dust—that is a far return.﴾ That is, they say: "When we die and decay, and our joints are scattered, and we become dust, how is it possible to return after that to this structure and composition?" ﴿That is a far return﴾: that is, far from occurring. The meaning of this is that they believe it impossible and not feasible.

Allah, Exalted, replied to them: ﴿We already know what the earth diminishes of them﴾: that is, what it consumes of their bodies in decay. We know that, and nothing is hidden from Us: where the bodies were scattered, where they went, and to where they arrived. ﴿And with Us is a preserved Book﴾: that is, one that preserves that. So His knowledge is comprehensive, and the Book also contains all things, precisely recorded.

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying ﴿We already know what the earth diminishes of them﴾: that is, what it eats of their flesh and skins, and their bones and hair. Likewise said Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and others.

Then Allah, exalted is He, explained the cause of their disbelief, their obstinacy, and their deeming unlikely what is not unlikely at all, so He said: ﴿Nay, they denied the truth when it came to them, so they are in a confused state.﴾ That is, this is the condition of everyone who departs from the truth; whatever such a person says afterward is false. "Marij" means what is varied, disordered, confused, and containing objectionable elements within it, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, you are in a contradictory saying. Turned away from it is whoever is turned away.﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 8, 9].

He, exalted is He, is directing His servants to His great power, by which He manifested something greater than what they wondered at and deemed unlikely to occur: ﴿Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We built it and adorned it, and it has no rifts?﴾ That is, adorned it with the lamps (of stars). ﴿And it has no rifts.﴾ Mujahid said: that is, no cracks. Others said: no openings. And others said: no fissures. The meanings are close to one another, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He who created seven heavens in layers. You see no discrepancy in the creation of the Most Merciful. So return your gaze; do you see any flaw? Then return your gaze twice; your gaze will return to you humbled, and it will be weary﴾ [Al-Mulk: 3, 4]. That is, fatigued, meaning unable to see any defect or deficiency.

* *

His saying: ﴿And the earth – We spread it out﴾, that is, We expanded it and laid it out as a bed. ﴿And We cast into it firm mountains﴾, which are the mountains, so that it would not sway with its inhabitants and tremble. For it is held steady over the flow of the water surrounding it from all its sides. ﴿And We caused to grow in it every beautiful pair﴾, that is, of all kinds of crops, fruits, plants and species. ﴿And of everything We created pairs, so that you may remember﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 49]. His saying: ﴿beautiful﴾ means good and fresh.

﴿As an insight and a reminder for every servant who turns back in repentance.﴾ That is: the observing of the creation of the heavens [and the earth] [[Addition from M, A.]] and what [Allah] [[Addition from A.]] placed in them of great signs is an insight, an indication, and a reminder for every servant who turns back in repentance, that is, one who is humble, fearful, trembling, and returns to Allah, mighty and majestic.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We sent down from the sky blessed water﴾, that is, beneficial. ﴿And We caused to grow by it gardens﴾, that is, orchards and the like. ﴿And grain of harvest﴾, which is the crop grown for its grain and for storage.

﴿And tall palm trees﴾, that is, tall and lofty. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Suddi and others said: "al-Basiqat" means the tall ones. ﴿With clustered spathes⁠﴾, that is, arranged in layers. ﴿As sustenance for the servants﴾, that is, for creation. ﴿And We gave life thereby to a dead land﴾, which is the earth that had been lifeless. When the water descended upon it, it stirred, swelled, and brought forth every beautiful pair, of blossoms and other things, whose beauty dazzles the eye, after it had no plant in it. Thus it became green and stirring. This is a parable of resurrection after death and destruction; in the same way Allah gives life to the dead. What is observed of His great power through the senses is greater than what the deniers of resurrection reject. Like His saying: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ [Ghafir: 57], and His saying: ﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and was not wearied by their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, indeed; He is over all things competent﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 33]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth barren; but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells. Indeed, He who revived it is the Reviver of the dead. Indeed, He is over all things competent﴾ [Fussilat: 39]. [[In M: "barren" (hamidah), which is an error.]]

Allah the Exalted says, warning the disbelievers of Quraysh about what He inflicted upon those like them, their counterparts and their peers among the deniers before them, of vengeance and painful punishment in this world. Such were the people of Nuh (Noah), and what Allah punished them with, the general drowning of all the people of the earth [[In manuscript M: "al-'azim" (the great)]], and the companions of the Rass (the well), whose story has already been mentioned in Surat al-Furqan (the Criterion) [[This was mentioned in Surat al-Furqan at verse (38).]]. ﴿And Thamud, and 'Ad, and Pharaoh, and the brothers of Lut﴾, who were his (Lut's) nation, to whom he was sent, from the people of Sodom and its neighbours, from the depths; and how Allah caused the earth to swallow them up and turned their land into a foul, putrid lake, because of their disbelief, their transgression and their opposition to the truth.

﴿And the companions of the Thicket﴾, who were the people of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him), ﴿and the people of Tubba'﴾, who was the Yemeni (king). We have already mentioned his situation in Surat al-Dukhan (the Smoke), which suffices so that it need not be repeated here, and to Allah belongs all praise.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 50, verses 16–22 (part 1 of 2):

God, exalted is He, informs about His power over the human being: that He created him, and that His knowledge encompasses all his affairs, to the extent that He knows what the souls of the children of Adam whisper to themselves, whether good or evil. It is established in the Sahih, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed God (ﷺ) has overlooked for my community what their souls whisper to them, as long as they do not speak it or act upon it." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5269, and Sahih Muslim, no. 127.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We are closer to him than the jugular vein﴾, it means: His angels are closer to the human being than the jugular vein is to him. Whoever interprets it as referring to knowledge has only fled from it so that there would not follow indwelling (hulul) or union (ittihad), and both are negated by consensus (ijma', the agreement of the scholars). Exalted is God and sanctified. But the wording does not require this, for He did not say: "And I am closer to him than the jugular vein," but rather He said: ﴿And We are closer to him﴾, just as He said regarding the dying person: ﴿And We are closer to him than you, but you do not see﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 85], meaning His angels. Likewise He said: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾ [al-Hijr: 9]; the angels sent down the Reminder, which is the Qur'an, by the permission of God, mighty and majestic. Likewise the angels are closer to the human being than the jugular vein is to him, by God's empowerment of them to do so. The angel has an inspiration (lammah) in the human being, just as Satan has an inspiration, and likewise: "Satan runs through the son of Adam as the blood runs," as the truthful and the believed one (ﷺ) informed. Therefore He said here: ﴿When the two receivers receive﴾, meaning the two angels who record the deeds of the human being. ﴿Seated on the right and on the left﴾, that is, watchful.

﴿He does not utter a word except that with him is an observer ready﴾, that is, the son of Adam does not utter a word, that is, does not speak a statement, except that there is someone with it who watches it, prepared for that, who records it. He leaves out no word and no movement, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And indeed, there are over you guardians, noble and recording, who know what you do﴾ [al-Infitar: 10–12].

The scholars have differed: Does the angel record every word of speech? This is the view of al-Hasan and Qatadah. Or does he record only what carries reward and punishment, as is the view of Ibn 'Abbas? These are two opinions. The apparent meaning of the verse is the first, because of the generality of His saying: ﴿He does not utter a word except that with him is an observer ready﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Alqamah al-Laythi narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather 'Alqamah, from Bilal ibn al-Harith al-Muzani, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed a man may speak a word of the good pleasure of God, the Exalted, which he does not think will reach what it has reached, and God writes for him by it His pleasure until the day he meets Him. And indeed a man may speak a word of the wrath of God, which he does not think will reach what it has reached, and God writes against him by it His wrath until the day he meets Him." He said: 'Alqamah used to say: "How many a statement has the hadith of Bilal ibn al-Harith prevented me from!"

It was also transmitted by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Muhammad ibn 'Amr with this chain. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih." It has a corroborating narration in the Sahih [the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 6478].

Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays said: The companion of the right records the good, and he is in authority over the companion of the left. If the servant commits a sin, he says to him: "Hold back." If he seeks God's forgiveness, the Exalted, he forbids him from recording it; and if he refuses, he records it. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said, reciting this verse: ﴿Seated on the right and on the left﴾: O son of Adam, a scroll has been unfolded for you, and two noble angels have been assigned to you, one on your right and the other on your left. As for the one on your right, he guards your good deeds, and as for the one on your left, he guards your evil deeds. So do what you wish, whether little or much, until when you die your scroll is rolled up and placed upon your neck with you in your grave, until you come forth on the Day of Resurrection. At that time He says: ﴿And every person's fate We have fastened to his neck, and We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record which he will find wide open. "Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as an accountant"﴾ [al-Isra': 13–14]. Then he said: "By God, just with you is the One who made you the reckoner of your own self."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿He does not utter a word except that with him is an observer ready﴾: He said: He records everything he speaks, whether good or bad, to the extent that he records his saying: "I ate, I drank, I went, I came, I saw." Then, when Thursday comes, his saying and his deed are presented; what is in it of good or bad is confirmed, and the rest is cast away. This is His saying: ﴿God effaces what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾ [al-Ra'd: 39].

It is also reported from Imam Ahmad that he was moaning during his illness, and it reached him from Tawus that he said: "The angel records everything, even the moaning." So Ahmad did not moan until he died, may God have mercy on him. [Narrated by Salih ibn Imam Ahmad in the biography of his father.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the agony of death has come in truth; that is what you were trying to avoid﴾. God, exalted is He, says: And the agony of death has come, O human being, in truth, that is, it has revealed to you the certainty about which you were in doubt. ﴿That is what you were trying to avoid﴾, that is: this is what you were fleeing from, and it has come to you; there is no escape and no refuge, no release and no deliverance.

The commentators have differed about who is addressed by His saying: ﴿And the agony of death has come in truth; that is what you were trying to avoid﴾. The correct view is that the one addressed is the human being as such. It has also been said: the disbeliever; and it has been said: other than that.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Ibrahim ibn Ziyad, Sablan, narrated to us; 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad informed us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Alqamah, from his father, from his grandfather 'Alqamah ibn Waqqas [in A: "Abi Waqqas," which is an error; see his biography in Tahdhib al-Tahdhib], that 'Aishah, may God be pleased with her, said: I was present with my father while he was dying, and I was sitting at his head. Then a faintness overcame him, and I recited a line of poetry:

"He whose tears are not ever restrained... indeed there will be a time when it is poured out [or: he will surely be struck once]."

She said: He raised his head and said: "O my daughter, it is not so, but rather as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the agony of death has come in truth; that is what you were trying to avoid﴾."

And Khalaf ibn Hisham narrated to us: Abu Shihab al-Khayyat narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Bahi, who said: When Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, became heavy [in his illness], 'Aishah, may God be pleased with her, came and recited this line of poetry:

"By your life, wealth does not benefit a man when the death rattle comes upon him one day and the chest is constricted."

He uncovered his face and said: "It is not so, but my saying is: ﴿And the agony of death has come in truth; that is what you were trying to avoid﴾." I have cited many chains for this report in the biography of the Siddiq at the mention of his death, may God be pleased with him.

It is established in the Sahih from the Prophet (ﷺ) that when death overcame him he began wiping the sweat from his face and saying: "Glory be to God! Indeed death has its agonies."

Regarding His saying: ﴿That is what you were trying to avoid﴾, there are two opinions:

The first: that "ma" here is a relative pronoun, meaning: "that which you were trying to avoid" (tahidu: to turn away, to keep distant, to flee), "has come upon you and descended into your courtyard."

The second view: that "ma" is a negative particle, meaning: "That is what you were not able to flee from nor to turn away from."

Al-Tabarani said in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Sa'igh al-Makki narrated to us; Hafs ibn 'Umar al-Hudayy narrated to us; Mu'adh ibn Muhammad al-Hudhali narrated to us, from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from al-Hasan, from Samurah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of one who flees from death is the likeness of the fox, which the earth pursues because of a debt. It comes running until, when it is exhausted and weary, it enters its burrow. Then the earth says to it: 'O fox, my debt!' So it comes out, and it has a limp, and it continues like this until its neck is severed and it dies." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (7/222). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (2/320): "In it is Mu'adh ibn Muhammad al-Hudhali. Al-'Uqayli said: his raising of this hadith is not followed."]

The meaning of this parable: just as there is no escape for the fox and no turning away from the earth, so too the human being has no turning away from death.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the Horn will be blown; that is the Day of the Threat﴾. The discussion of the hadith concerning the blowing of the Horn, the terror, the swoon and the resurrection has already preceded, and that is the Day of Resurrection. In a hadith, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "How can I be at ease when the one with the horn has put the horn to his lips, bent his forehead, and is waiting for permission to be given?" They said: "O Messenger of God, what should we say?" He said: "Say: 'God is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs.'" The people then said: "God is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs."

﴿And every soul will come, with it a driver and a witness﴾, that is: an angel who drives it to the place of gathering, and an angel who bears witness against it concerning its deeds. This is the apparent meaning of the noble verse, and it is the preference of Ibn Jarir. Then it was related from the hadith of Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Yahya ibn Rafi', a client of the Thaqif tribe, who said: I heard 'Uthman ibn 'Affan giving a sermon, and he recited this verse: ﴿And every soul will come, with it a driver and a witness﴾, and he said: "A driver who drives it to God, and a witness who bears witness against it for what it did." Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said likewise.

Mutarrif said, from Abu Ja'far, a client of Ashja', from Abu Hurairah: the driver is the angel, and the witness is the deed. Likewise al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said.

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: the driver is from the angels, and the witness is the human being himself, who bears witness against himself. Al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim also said this.

Ibn Jarir related three opinions regarding who is intended by this address in His saying: ﴿You were certainly in heedlessness of this, so We have removed from you your covering, and your sight today is sharp﴾.

The first: that what is meant is the disbeliever. This was narrated by 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn 'Abbas, and al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim and Salih ibn Kaysan say this.

The second: that what is meant is every person, whether righteous or wicked, because the Hereafter in relation to this world is like wakefulness, and this world is like sleep. This is the preference of Ibn Jarir, and he related it from Husayn ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abbas.

The third: that the one addressed is the Prophet (ﷺ). This is the view of Zayd ibn Aslam and his son. According to their view, the meaning is: "You were certainly in heedlessness of this matter before it was revealed to you, so We removed your covering by sending it down to you, and your sight today is sharp."

The apparent context indicates otherwise: rather, the address is to the human being as such (min haythu huwa). By His saying: ﴿You were heedless of this﴾, it means: of this Day. ﴿So We have removed from you your covering, and your sight today is sharp﴾, i.e., strong. This is because every person on the Day of Resurrection will be clear-sighted, and even the disbelievers in this world will, on the Day of Resurrection, be upright [in their perception], but that will not benefit them. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Hear them and see them, the Day they come to Us﴾ [Maryam: 38]. And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿If only you could see when the criminals hang their heads before their Lord, saying, "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us [to the world] that we may do righteousness; indeed, we are certain"﴾ [As-Sajdah: 12].

"He whose tears are not ever restrained... indeed there will be a time when it is poured out [or: he will surely be struck once]."

[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5269, and Sahih Muslim, no. 127.]

Exalted is God and sanctified. Likewise the angels are closer to the human being than the jugular vein is to him, by God's empowerment of them to do so. The angel has an inspiration (lammah) in the human being, just as Satan has an inspiration, and likewise: "Satan runs through the son of Adam as the blood runs," as the truthful and the believed one (ﷺ) informed. Therefore He said here: ﴿When the two receivers receive﴾, meaning the two angels who record the deeds of the human being. ﴿Seated on the right and on the left﴾, that is, watchful.

﴿He does not utter a word except that with him is an observer ready﴾, that is, the son of Adam does not utter a word, that is, does not speak a statement, except that there is someone with it who watches it, prepared for that, who records it. He leaves out no word and no movement, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And indeed, there are over you guardians, noble and recording, who know what you do﴾ [al-Infitar: 10–12].

And indeed a man may speak a word of the wrath of God, which he does not think will reach what it has reached, and God writes against him by it His wrath until the day he meets Him." He said: 'Alqamah used to say: "How many a statement has the hadith of Bilal ibn al-Harith prevented me from!"

It was also transmitted by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Muhammad ibn 'Amr with this chain. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih." If he seeks God's forgiveness, the Exalted, he forbids him from recording it; and if he refuses, he records it. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said, reciting this verse: ﴿Seated on the right and on the left﴾: O son of Adam, a scroll has been unfolded for you, and two noble angels have been assigned to you, one on your right and the other on your left. As for the one on your right, he guards your good deeds, and as for the one on your left, he guards your evil deeds. So do what you wish, whether little or much, until when you die your scroll is rolled up and placed upon your neck with you in your grave, until you come forth on the Day of Resurrection. At that time He says: ﴿And every person's fate We have fastened to his neck, and We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record which he will find wide open. "Read your record. So Ahmad did not moan until he died, may God have mercy on him. [Narrated by Salih ibn Imam Ahmad in the biography of his father.]

He uncovered his face and said: "It is not so, but my saying is: ﴿And the agony of death has come in truth; that is what you were trying to avoid﴾." I have cited many chains for this report in the biography of the Siddiq at the mention of his death, may God be pleased with him.

The second view: that "ma" is a negative particle, meaning: "That is what you were not able to flee from nor to turn away from."

* *

God, exalted is He, informs about His power over the human being: that He created him, and that His knowledge encompasses all his affairs, to the extent that He knows what the souls of the children of Adam whisper to themselves, whether good or evil. It is established in the Sahih, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed God (ﷺ) has overlooked for my community what their souls whisper to them, as long as they do not speak it or act upon it." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5269, and Sahih Muslim, no. 127.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We are closer to him than the jugular vein﴾, it means: His angels are closer to the human being than the jugular vein is to him. Exalted is God and sanctified. But the wording does not require this, for He did not say: "And I am closer to him than the jugular vein," but rather He said: ﴿And We are closer to him﴾, just as He said regarding the dying person: ﴿And We are closer to him than you, but you do not see﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 85], meaning His angels. Likewise He said: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾ [al-Hijr: 9]; the angels sent down the Reminder, which is the Qur'an, by the permission of God, mighty and majestic. Likewise the angels are closer to the human being than the jugular vein is to him, by God's empowerment of them to do so. The angel has an inspiration (lammah) in the human being, just as Satan has an inspiration, and likewise: "Satan runs through the son of Adam as the blood runs," as the truthful and the believed one (ﷺ) informed. Therefore He said here: ﴿When the two receivers receive﴾, meaning the two angels who record the deeds of the human being. ﴿Seated on the right and on the left﴾, that is, watchful.

﴿He does not utter a word except that with him is an observer ready﴾, that is, the son of Adam does not utter a word, that is, does not speak a statement, except that there is someone with it who watches it, prepared for that, who records it. He leaves out no word and no movement, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And indeed, there are over you guardians, noble and recording, who know what you do﴾ [al-Infitar: 10–12].

The scholars have differed: Does the angel record every word of speech? This is the view of al-Hasan and Qatadah. Or does he record only what carries reward and punishment, as is the view of Ibn 'Abbas? These are two opinions. The apparent meaning of the verse is the first, because of the generality of His saying: ﴿He does not utter a word except that with him is an observer ready﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Alqamah al-Laythi narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather 'Alqamah, from Bilal ibn al-Harith al-Muzani, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed a man may speak a word of the good pleasure of God, the Exalted, which he does not think will reach what it has reached, and God writes for him by it His pleasure until the day he meets Him. And indeed a man may speak a word of the wrath of God, which he does not think will reach what it has reached, and God writes against him by it His wrath until the day he meets Him." He said: 'Alqamah used to say: "How many a statement has the hadith of Bilal ibn al-Harith prevented me from!"

It was also transmitted by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Muhammad ibn 'Amr with this chain. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih." It has a corroborating narration in the Sahih [the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 6478].

Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays said: The companion of the right records the good, and he is in authority over the companion of the left. If the servant commits a sin, he says to him: "Hold back." If he seeks God's forgiveness, the Exalted, he forbids him from recording it; and if he refuses, he records it. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said, reciting this verse: ﴿Seated on the right and on the left﴾: O son of Adam, a scroll has been unfolded for you, and two noble angels have been assigned to you, one on your right and the other on your left. As for the one on your right, he guards your good deeds, and as for the one on your left, he guards your evil deeds. So do what you wish, whether little or much, until when you die your scroll is rolled up and placed upon your neck with you in your grave, until you come forth on the Day of Resurrection. At that time He says: ﴿And every person's fate We have fastened to his neck, and We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record which he will find wide open. "Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as an accountant"﴾ [al-Isra': 13–14]. Then he said: "By God, just with you is the One who made you the reckoner of your own self."

Then, when Thursday comes, his saying and his deed are presented; what is in it of good or bad is confirmed, and the rest is cast away. This is His saying: ﴿God effaces what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾ [al-Ra'd: 39].

It is also reported from Imam Ahmad that he was moaning during his illness, and it reached him from Tawus that he said: "The angel records everything, even the moaning." So Ahmad did not moan until he died, may God have mercy on him. [Narrated by Salih ibn Imam Ahmad in the biography of his father.]

* *

Then a faintness overcame him, and I recited a line of poetry:

"He whose tears are not ever restrained... indeed there will be a time when it is poured out [or: he will surely be struck once]."

She said: He raised his head and said: "O my daughter, it is not so, but rather as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the agony of death has come in truth; that is what you were trying to avoid﴾."

Allah, exalted is He, says, informing about the angel assigned to the deeds of the son of Adam, that he will bear witness against him on the Day of Resurrection concerning what he did [[In A: "بما عمل" (bima 'amila), "what he did."]], and he will say: ﴿This is what is ready with me.﴾ That is: prepared and present, with no addition and no subtraction.

Mujahid said: This is the speech of the driving angel (al-sa'iq), who says: "This is the son of Adam whom You assigned to me; I have brought him forward."

Ibn Jarir chose that the words cover both the driver (al-sa'iq) and the witness (al-shahid), and his view has direction and strength.

Then Allah, exalted is He, judges among the creation with justice, saying: ﴿Throw into Hell every stubborn disbeliever.﴾

The grammarians (al-nuhat) differed concerning His words ﴿Throw﴾ (alqiya). Some of them said: it is a dialect of some Arabs who address a single person in the dual form, as it is narrated of al-Hajjaj that he used to say: "O guard, strike his neck (idribā 'unuqahu)." Among the verses Ibn Jarir recited as evidence for this dialect is the poet's saying:

"If you two restrain me, O son of Affan, I will be restrained; and if you two leave me, I will defend an honour that is protected."

It was also said: rather, it is the nun of emphasis (nun al-ta'kid), made light and turned into an alif. This is far-fetched, because that occurs only in pausal form (al-waqf), and the apparent meaning is that it is addressed to the driver and the witness. The driver brought him to the place of reckoning, and when the witness had testified against him, Allah, exalted is He, commanded the two of them to cast him into the Fire of Hell, and wretched is the destination.

﴿Throw into Hell every stubborn disbeliever.﴾ That is: one who greatly disbelieves and denies the truth. ﴿Stubborn (ʿanid)﴾: one who opposes the truth and confronts it with falsehood while knowing it. ﴿Who forbids the good﴾: he does not fulfil what is due upon him of rights, and there is in him no righteousness, no maintaining of ties, and no charity. ﴿Transgressor (mu'tad)﴾: in what he spends and disposes of, exceeding the limit in it.

Qatadah said: "Transgressor" in his speech, his conduct, and his affairs.

﴿Doubter (murib)﴾: one who is in doubt about his matter, and is a cause of doubt for whoever looks into his affair.

﴿Who set up with Allah another god﴾: he associated others with Allah and worshipped another alongside Him. ﴿Then cast him into the severe punishment.﴾

It has already been mentioned in a hadith that a neck (ʿunuq) of Fire will emerge before the creatures, calling out with a voice that the creatures hear: "I have been assigned to three: to every tyrant, to whoever set up another god with Allah, and to the image-makers." Then it will coil around them.

Imam Ahmad said: Mu'awiyah—that is Ibn Hisham—narrated to us: Shaiban narrated to us, from Firas, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "A neck will come out of the Fire, speaking, saying: 'I have been assigned today to three: to every tyrant, to whoever set up another god with Allah, and to whoever killed a soul without a soul [[In M: "حق" (haqq), "without a right."]]. It will coil around them and hurl them into the depths of Hell.'"

﴿His companion will say﴾: Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, and others said: he is the devil (shaytan) assigned to him. ﴿Our Lord, I did not make him transgress﴾: that is, he says about the human being who has arrived at the Resurrection as a disbeliever, that his devil disowns him, and says: ﴿Our Lord, I did not make him transgress﴾, meaning: I did not lead him astray. ﴿But he was in far-off error﴾: rather, he was in himself astray, ready to accept falsehood, opposed to the truth. As Allah, exalted is He, informed in another verse, in His words: ﴿And Satan will say when the matter has been decided: Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you. I had no authority over you except that I called you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I disbelieved in your associating me [with Allah] before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment.﴾ [Ibrahim: 22]

* *

As for His words: ﴿Do not dispute before Me﴾, the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says this to the human and his companion from the jinn. That is because the two of them dispute before the Truth. The human says: "O Lord, this one led me astray from the Reminder after it had come to me." And the devil says: ﴿Our Lord, I did not make him transgress, but he was in far-off error﴾, that is, far from the path of truth. Then the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says to them: ﴿Do not dispute before Me﴾, that is, in My presence, ﴿and I had already presented to you the warning﴾, that is, I had already given you notice through the tongues of the messengers, sent down the books, and the proofs, clear evidence and demonstrations were established against you.

﴿The word is not changed before Me﴾. Mujahid said: this means that I have already decided what I am to decide. ﴿And I am not unjust to the servants﴾: that is, I do not punish anyone for another's sin; rather, I do not punish anyone except for his own sin, after the proof has been established against him.

﴿His companion will say﴾: Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, and others said: he is the devil (shaytan) assigned to him. ﴿Our Lord, I did not make him transgress﴾: that is, he says about the human being who has arrived at the Resurrection as a disbeliever, that his devil disowns him, and says: ﴿Our Lord, I did not make him transgress﴾, meaning: I did not lead him astray. ﴿But he was in far-off error﴾: rather, he was in himself astray, ready to accept falsehood, opposed to the truth. As Allah, exalted is He, informed in another verse, in His words: ﴿And Satan will say when the matter has been decided: Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you. I had no authority over you except that I called you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I disbelieved in your associating me [with Allah] before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment.﴾ [Ibrahim: 22]

* *

As for His words: ﴿Do not dispute before Me﴾, the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says this to the human and his companion from the jinn. That is because the two of them dispute before the Truth. The human says: "O Lord, this one led me astray from the Reminder after it had come to me." And the devil says: ﴿Our Lord, I did not make him transgress, but he was in far-off error﴾, that is, far from the path of truth. Then the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, says to them: ﴿Do not dispute before Me﴾, that is, in My presence, ﴿and I had already presented to you the warning﴾, that is, I had already given you notice through the tongues of the messengers, sent down the books, and the proofs, clear evidence and demonstrations were established against you.

﴿The word is not changed before Me﴾. Mujahid said: this means that I have already decided what I am to decide. ﴿And I am not unjust to the servants﴾: that is, I do not punish anyone for another's sin; rather, I do not punish anyone except for his own sin, after the proof has been established against him.

Ibn Kathir says that Allah, exalted is He, tells Hell on the Day of Resurrection: "Are you filled?" This is because He promised that He would fill it with jinn and mankind, all of them. He, glory be to Him, commands whoever He commands to be cast into it, and it is thrown in while it says: ﴿Is there any more?﴾ That is, "Is there anything left that you can add to me?" This is the apparent meaning of the context of the verse, and the hadiths point to it:

Al-Bukhari, commenting on this verse, said: Abdullah ibn Abi al-Aswad narrated to us, Harami ibn 'Umara narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "It is cast into the Fire, and it says: 'Is there any more?' until He places His foot in it, and it says: 'Qat, qat (enough, enough).'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4848.]

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Jahannam will continue to have people cast into it, and it will say: 'Is there any more?' until the Lord of Might places His foot in it, whereupon some of it draws in upon the other, and it says: 'Qat, qat, by Your might and Your generosity!' And Paradise will continue to have surplus, until Allah creates for it another creation, and He will settle them in the surplus of Paradise." [Al-Musnad, 3/234.]

Then Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Qatadah, in similar wording. [Sahih Muslim, no. 4848.] And Aban al-Attar and Sulayman al-Taymi narrated it from Qatadah, in similar wording. [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir, 26/106.]

Another hadith: Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Qattan narrated to us, Abu Sufyan al-Himyari Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Awf narrated to us, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, who raised it (to the Prophet), though Abu Sufyan mostly stopped it at Abu Hurayrah: "It is said to Jahannam: 'Are you filled?' and it says: 'Is there any more?' Then the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, places His foot upon it, and it says: 'Qat, qat.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4849.]

It was narrated by Ayyub and Hisham ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, with the same. [Ahmad in his Musnad (2/507) by way of Hisham ibn Hassan; al-Tabari in his Tafsir (26/107) by way of Ayyub and Hisham ibn Hassan.]

Another route: Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Paradise and the Fire disputed. The Fire said: 'I have been given the arrogant and the haughty.' Paradise said: 'What is it with me that only the weak among people and their lowly enter me?' Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said to Paradise: 'You are My mercy; I show mercy through you to whomever I will of My servants.' And He said to the Fire: 'You are only My punishment; I punish through you whomever I will of My servants, and each of you will have its fill. As for the Fire, it will not be filled until He places His foot upon it, whereupon it says: "Qat, qat," and then it is filled, and some of it draws in upon the other, and Allah does not wrong any of His creation. As for Paradise, Allah will create for it another creation.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4850.]

Another hadith: Muslim said in his Sahih: Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Paradise and the Fire disputed. The Fire said: 'In me are the tyrants and the arrogant.' Paradise said: 'In me are the weak among people and their poor.' He judged between them, and said to Paradise: 'You are only My mercy; I show mercy through you to whomever I will of My servants.' And He said to the Fire: 'You are only My punishment; I punish through you whomever I will of My servants, and each of you will have its fill.'" Muslim alone narrated it by this route, not al-Bukhari. [Sahih Muslim, no. 2847.] And Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad narrated it by another route, from Abu Sa'id, with a fuller version, saying:

Hasan and Rawh narrated to us, both said: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Paradise and the Fire boasted. The Fire said: 'O Lord, there enter me the tyrants, the arrogant, the kings and the nobles.' Paradise said: 'O Lord, there enter me the weak, the poor and the needy.' Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says to the Fire: 'You are My punishment; I afflict with you whomever I will.' And He said to Paradise: 'You are My mercy, you encompass everything, and each of you will have its fill. Those of the Fire will be cast into it, and it says: "Is there any more?" He said: And it is cast into it, and it says: "Is there any more?" And it is cast into it, and it says: "Is there any more?" until its Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, comes to it and places His foot upon it, whereupon it draws in and says: "Enough, enough!" As for Paradise, it will remain with whatever Allah wills it to remain, and then Allah creates for it a creation as He wills.'" [Al-Musnad, 3/13.]

Another hadith: Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said in his Musnad: Uqbah ibn Mukram narrated to us, Yunus narrated to us, Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from Udi ibn Thabit, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will make Himself known to me on the Day of Resurrection, and I will prostrate in a prostration by which He will be pleased with me. Then I will praise Him with a praise by which He will be pleased with me. Then I will be permitted to speak. Then my Ummah will pass over the Sirat, which is laid between the backs of Jahannam, and they will pass faster than the glance and the arrow, and faster than the best of horses, until a man comes out of it crawling, and those are their deeds. Jahannam will be asking for more, until He places His foot in it, whereupon some of it draws in upon the other and it says: 'Qat, qat!' And I will be at the Pool." It was said: "What is the Pool, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, its drink is whiter than milk, sweeter than honey, colder than snow, and its scent is better than musk. Its vessels are more numerous than the stars; whoever drinks from it will never thirst again, and it will never be withheld from anyone so that he is never satisfied." [Ibn Abi Asim in al-Sunnah, no. 790, by way of Uqbah ibn Mukram. Al-Albani said: "Its isnad is fabricated; its fault is Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim, Abu Maryam al-Ansari, who used to fabricate hadith, as said by Ibn al-Madini and Abu Dawud."] This view is the one chosen by Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Yahya al-Hammani narrated to us, from Nadr al-Khazzaz, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿On the Day We say to Jahannam, "Are you filled?" and it says, "Is there any more?"﴾ He said: "It has not been filled." He said: "It says: 'Is there in me any place that can be added to me?'"

Similarly al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated from Ikrimah regarding ﴿and it says, "Is there any more?"﴾: "Is there in one place of entry, which has been filled?"

Al-Walid ibn Muslim said, from Yazid ibn Abi Maryam, that he heard Mujahid say: "It will continue to be thrown into it until it says: 'I am filled,' and it says: 'Is there any more in me?'" And from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, something similar.

According to these scholars, the words of Allah, exalted is He, ﴿Are you filled?﴾ refer only to after He places His foot upon it, whereupon it draws in and says at that time: "Is there any remaining space in me that can hold anything?"

Al-Awfi said, from Ibn Abbas: "That is when there is no place left in it that can hold even a needle." And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous, not far away﴾: Qatadah, Abu Malik and al-Suddi said: ﴿brought near﴾ means it will be brought close and made nigh to the righteous, ﴿not far away﴾, and that is on the Day of Resurrection; it is not far, because it is certain to come, and everything that is to come is coming.

﴿This is what you were promised, for every constantly returning, watchful one﴾ [In A: "awwab hafiz"]: that is, one who returns repeatedly, repents, and desists. ﴿Watchful﴾: one who guards the covenant, so does not break or violate it.

Ubayd ibn Umayr said: "The awwab is the watchful one who does not sit in a gathering [and then rise] until he seeks forgiveness from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

﴿Who feared the Most Merciful unseen﴾: that is, who feared Allah in his secret, where no one sees him except Allah, as the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "And a man who remembers Allah in private, and his eyes overflow."

﴿And came with a heart turned in repentance﴾: that is, he meets Allah on the Day of Resurrection with a sound heart, turned in repentance to Him, humbled before Him.

﴿Enter it in peace﴾: that is, Paradise. Qatadah said: "They are safe from the punishment of Allah, and the angels of Allah greet them."

* *

As for His words: ﴿That is the Day of Eternity﴾: that is, they will abide forever in Paradise; they will never die, never leave, and never seek to be moved from it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿For them is whatever they will therein﴾: that is, whatever kind of pleasures they choose and seek, it will be brought to them.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Amr ibn Uthman narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, from Bahir ibn Sa'd, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Kathir ibn Murrah, who said: "Among the increase [al-mazid] is that a cloud passes over the people of Paradise and says: 'What do you want, that I may rain it down for you?' They do not ask for anything except that it rains it upon them." Kuthayyir said: "If Allah makes me witness that, I will surely say: 'Rain upon us, O maidens adorned.'"

And in a hadith from Ibn Mas'ud, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Indeed you will desire birds in Paradise, and one will fall before you roasted." [Narrated by al-Hasan ibn Arafah in his Juz' (22), al-Bazzar in his Musnad (3532, Kashf al-Astar), and Ibn Adi in al-Kamil (6/689), by way of Khalaf ibn Khalifah, from Humayd al-A'raj, from Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn Mas'ud, raised. In its isnad is Humayd al-A'raj; al-Bukhari said: "munkar al-hadith," and Ibn Hibban said: "his hadiths resemble fabrications."]

Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Amir al-Ahwal, from Abu al-Siddiq [in M: "from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq"], from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If the believer desires a child in Paradise, its pregnancy, birth and growing up will happen in a single hour."

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, from Bundar, from Mu'adh ibn Hisham, with the same. [Al-Musnad (3/9); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2563; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 4338.] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib," and he added "as he desires."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And with Us is more﴾: like His words, exalted is He: ﴿For those who did good is the best reward and more﴾ [Yunus: 26]. It has already been mentioned in Sahih Muslim, from Suhayb ibn Sinan al-Rumi, that it is the looking upon the Noble Face of Allah. Al-Bazzar and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated, from the hadith of Sharik al-Qadi, from Uthman ibn Umayr Abu al-Yaqzan, from Anas ibn Malik, regarding the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And with Us is more﴾: He said: "The Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, will manifest Himself to them every Friday."

Al-Imam Abu Abdullah al-Shafi'i also narrated it as a marfu' hadith, saying in his Musnad: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad informed us; Musa ibn Ubayda narrated to me; Abu al-Azhar Mu'awiyah ibn Ishaq ibn Talha narrated to me, from Abd Allah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr [In M: "from Ubayd Allah ibn Umayr", while in the original: "Abd Allah Umayr"; the correction is from al-Shafi'i's al-Umm.] that he heard Anas ibn Malik say: Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah with a white mirror in which there was a spot, and the Prophet [In M: "Messenger of Allah".] ﷺ said: "What is this?" He said: "This is Friday, which you and your community have been favoured with. The people are followers of you in it: the Jews and the Christians. And for you in it is goodness, and for you in it is an hour in which no believing servant meets it while calling upon Allah for some good except that it is answered for him, and it is, with us, the Day of Increase (Yawm al-Mazid)." The Prophet ﷺ said: "O Jibril, and what is the Day of Increase?" He said: "Your Lord has taken in al-Firdaws a wide valley in which there are mounds of musk. When it is the day of Friday, Allah sends down whomever He wills [In M: "people".] of His angels, and around Him are pulpits of light, upon which are the seats of the Prophets, and those pulpits are surrounded by pulpits of gold, adorned with rubies and chrysolite, upon which are the martyrs and the truthful [In A: "the righteous".], and they sit behind them upon those mounds. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am your Lord, I have fulfilled My promise to you, so ask Me and I will give you.' They say: 'Our Lord, we ask You for Your pleasure.' He says: 'I am pleased with you, and for you is what you have wished for, and with Me is increase.' So they love Friday because of the good their Lord gives them in it, and it is the day on which your Lord settled upon the Throne, and in it Adam was created, and in it the Hour will be established."

Thus al-Imam al-Shafi'i narrated it in the chapter "al-Jumu'ah" of al-Umm [al-Umm (1/185).], and it has chains from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him. Ibn Jarir also reported this from the narration of Uthman ibn Umayr, from Anas, in a fuller form than this [Tafsir al-Tabari (26/109).]. He also mentioned here a lengthy report from Anas ibn Malik as a mawquf narration, and in it are many strange (gharib) elements [Tafsir al-Tabari (26/109).].

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us; Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us; Darraj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Indeed a man in Paradise will recline in Paradise for seventy years before he moves. Then a woman will come to him and strike his shoulder, and he will look at his face in her cheek, clearer than a mirror. And indeed the smallest pearl upon her illuminates what is between the East and the West. She will greet him, and he will return the greeting, and he will ask her: 'Who are you?' She will say: 'I am of the Mazid.' Upon her are seventy garments, the least of which is like al-Nu'man of Tuba, and his sight will penetrate them until he sees the marrow of her shin from behind all that. And upon her are crowns; indeed the smallest pearl among them illuminates what is between the East and the West." [Al-Musnad (3/75), in which: Darraj from Abu al-Haytham, weak (da'if).]

Likewise, Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated it from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Darraj, with the same [Reported by al-Tabari in his tafsir (26/110), and the discussion on it is like the preceding.].

Ibn Kathir says that Allah, exalted is He, tells Hell on the Day of Resurrection: "Are you filled?" This is because He promised that He would fill it with jinn and mankind, all of them. He, glory be to Him, commands whoever He commands to be cast into it, and it is thrown in while it says: ﴿Is there any more?﴾ That is, "Is there anything left that you can add to me?" This is the apparent meaning of the context of the verse, and the hadiths point to it:

Al-Bukhari, commenting on this verse, said: Abdullah ibn Abi al-Aswad narrated to us, Harami ibn 'Umara narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "It is cast into the Fire, and it says: 'Is there any more?' until He places His foot in it, and it says: 'Qat, qat (enough, enough).'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4848.]

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Jahannam will continue to have people cast into it, and it will say: 'Is there any more?' until the Lord of Might places His foot in it, whereupon some of it draws in upon the other, and it says: 'Qat, qat, by Your might and Your generosity!' And Paradise will continue to have surplus, until Allah creates for it another creation, and He will settle them in the surplus of Paradise." [Al-Musnad, 3/234.]

Then Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Qatadah, in similar wording. [Sahih Muslim, no. 4848.] And Aban al-Attar and Sulayman al-Taymi narrated it from Qatadah, in similar wording. [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir, 26/106.]

Another hadith: Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Qattan narrated to us, Abu Sufyan al-Himyari Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Awf narrated to us, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, who raised it (to the Prophet), though Abu Sufyan mostly stopped it at Abu Hurayrah: "It is said to Jahannam: 'Are you filled?' and it says: 'Is there any more?' Then the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, places His foot upon it, and it says: 'Qat, qat.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4849.]

It was narrated by Ayyub and Hisham ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, with the same. [Ahmad in his Musnad (2/507) by way of Hisham ibn Hassan; al-Tabari in his Tafsir (26/107) by way of Ayyub and Hisham ibn Hassan.]

Another route: Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Paradise and the Fire disputed. The Fire said: 'I have been given the arrogant and the haughty.' Paradise said: 'What is it with me that only the weak among people and their lowly enter me?' Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said to Paradise: 'You are My mercy; I show mercy through you to whomever I will of My servants.' And He said to the Fire: 'You are only My punishment; I punish through you whomever I will of My servants, and each of you will have its fill. Another hadith: Muslim said in his Sahih: Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Paradise and the Fire disputed. The Fire said: 'In me are the tyrants and the arrogant.' Paradise said: 'In me are the weak among people and their poor.' He judged between them, and said to Paradise: 'You are only My mercy; I show mercy through you to whomever I will of My servants.' And He said to the Fire: 'You are only My punishment; I punish through you whomever I will of My servants, and each of you will have its fill.'" Imam Ahmad narrated it by another route, from Abu Sa'id, with a fuller version, saying:

Hasan and Rawh narrated to us, both said: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Paradise and the Fire boasted. The Fire said: 'O Lord, there enter me the tyrants, the arrogant, the kings and the nobles.' Paradise said: 'O Lord, there enter me the weak, the poor and the needy.' Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says to the Fire: 'You are My punishment; I afflict with you whomever I will.' And He said to Paradise: 'You are My mercy, you encompass everything, and each of you will have its fill. Those of the Fire will be cast into it, and it says: "Is there any more?" He said: And it is cast into it, and it says: "Is there any more?" And it is cast into it, and it says: "Is there any more?" until its Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, comes to it and places His foot upon it, whereupon it draws in and says: "Enough, enough!" As for Paradise, it will remain with whatever Allah wills it to remain, and then Allah creates for it a creation as He wills.'" [Al-Musnad, 3/13.]

Another hadith: Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said in his Musnad: Uqbah ibn Mukram narrated to us, Yunus narrated to us, Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from Udi ibn Thabit, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will make Himself known to me on the Day of Resurrection, and I will prostrate in a prostration by which He will be pleased with me. Then I will praise Him with a praise by which He will be pleased with me. Then I will be permitted to speak. Then my Ummah will pass over the Sirat, which is laid between the backs of Jahannam, and they will pass faster than the glance and the arrow, and faster than the best of horses, until a man comes out of it crawling, and those are their deeds. Jahannam will be asking for more, until He places His foot in it, whereupon some of it draws in upon the other and it says: 'Qat, qat!' And I will be at the Pool." It was said: "What is the Pool, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, its drink is whiter than milk, sweeter than honey, colder than snow, and its scent is better than musk. Its vessels are more numerous than the stars; whoever drinks from it will never thirst again, and it will never be withheld from anyone so that he is never satisfied." [Ibn Abi Asim in al-Sunnah, no. 790, by way of Uqbah ibn Mukram. Al-Albani said: "Its isnad is fabricated; its fault is Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim, Abu Maryam al-Ansari, who used to fabricate hadith, as said by Ibn al-Madini and Abu Dawud."] This view is the one chosen by Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Yahya al-Hammani narrated to us, from Nadr al-Khazzaz, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿On the Day We say to Jahannam, "Are you filled?" and it says, "Is there any more?"﴾ He said: "It has not been filled." He said: "It says: 'Is there in me any place that can be added to me?'"

Similarly al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated from Ikrimah regarding ﴿and it says, "Is there any more?"﴾: "Is there in one place of entry, which has been filled?"

Al-Walid ibn Muslim said, from Yazid ibn Abi Maryam, that he heard Mujahid say: "It will continue to be thrown into it until it says: 'I am filled,' and it says: 'Is there any more in me?'" And from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, something similar.

Al-Awfi said, from Ibn Abbas: "That is when there is no place left in it that can hold even a needle." And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous, not far away﴾: Qatadah, Abu Malik and al-Suddi said: ﴿brought near﴾ means it will be brought close and made nigh to the righteous, ﴿not far away﴾, and that is on the Day of Resurrection; it is not far, because it is certain to come, and everything that is to come is coming.

﴿This is what you were promised, for every constantly returning, watchful one﴾ [In A: "awwab hafiz"]: that is, one who returns repeatedly, repents, and desists. ﴿Watchful﴾: one who guards the covenant, so does not break or violate it.

Ubayd ibn Umayr said: "The awwab is the watchful one who does not sit in a gathering [and then rise] until he seeks forgiveness from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

﴿Who feared the Most Merciful unseen﴾: that is, who feared Allah in his secret, where no one sees him except Allah, as the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "And a man who remembers Allah in private, and his eyes overflow."

﴿And came with a heart turned in repentance﴾: that is, he meets Allah on the Day of Resurrection with a sound heart, turned in repentance to Him, humbled before Him.

﴿Enter it in peace﴾: that is, Paradise. Qatadah said: "They are safe from the punishment of Allah, and the angels of Allah greet them."

* *

As for His words: ﴿That is the Day of Eternity﴾: that is, they will abide forever in Paradise; they will never die, never leave, and never seek to be moved from it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿For them is whatever they will therein﴾: that is, whatever kind of pleasures they choose and seek, it will be brought to them.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Amr ibn Uthman narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, from Bahir ibn Sa'd, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Kathir ibn Murrah, who said: "Among the increase [al-mazid] is that a cloud passes over the people of Paradise and says: 'What do you want, that I may rain it down for you?' They do not ask for anything except that it rains it upon them." Kuthayyir said: "If Allah makes me witness that, I will surely say: 'Rain upon us, O maidens adorned.'"

And in a hadith from Ibn Mas'ud, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Indeed you will desire birds in Paradise, and one will fall before you roasted." [Narrated by al-Hasan ibn Arafah in his Juz' (22), al-Bazzar in his Musnad (3532, Kashf al-Astar), and Ibn Adi in al-Kamil (6/689), by way of Khalaf ibn Khalifah, from Humayd al-A'raj, from Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn Mas'ud, raised. In its isnad is Humayd al-A'raj; al-Bukhari said: "munkar al-hadith," and Ibn Hibban said: "his hadiths resemble fabrications."]

Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Amir al-Ahwal, from Abu al-Siddiq [in M: "from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq"], from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If the believer desires a child in Paradise, its pregnancy, birth and growing up will happen in a single hour."

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, from Bundar, from Mu'adh ibn Hisham, with the same. [Al-Musnad (3/9); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2563; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 4338.] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib," and he added "as he desires."

* *

When it is the day of Friday, Allah sends down whomever He wills [In M: "people".] of His angels, and around Him are pulpits of light, upon which are the seats of the Prophets, and those pulpits are surrounded by pulpits of gold, adorned with rubies and chrysolite, upon which are the martyrs and the truthful [In A: "the righteous".], and they sit behind them upon those mounds. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am your Lord, I have fulfilled My promise to you, so ask Me and I will give you.' They say: 'Our Lord, we ask You for Your pleasure.' He says: 'I am pleased with you, and for you is what you have wished for, and with Me is increase.'
