He also mentioned here a lengthy report from Anas ibn Malik as a mawquf narration, and in it are many strange (gharib) elements [Tafsir al-Tabari (26/109).].

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us; Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us; Darraj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Indeed a man in Paradise will recline in Paradise for seventy years before he moves. Then a woman will come to him and strike his shoulder, and he will look at his face in her cheek, clearer than a mirror. And indeed the smallest pearl upon her illuminates what is between the East and the West. She will greet him, and he will return the greeting, and he will ask her: 'Who are you?' She will say: 'I am of the Mazid.' Upon her are seventy garments, the least of which is like al-Nu'man of Tuba, and his sight will penetrate them until he sees the marrow of her shin from behind all that. And upon her are crowns; indeed the smallest pearl among them illuminates what is between the East and the West." [Al-Musnad (3/75), in which: Darraj from Abu al-Haytham, weak (da'if).]

Likewise, Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated it from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Darraj, with the same [Reported by al-Tabari in his tafsir (26/110), and the discussion on it is like the preceding.].

Ibn Kathir says that Allah, exalted is He, tells Hell on the Day of Resurrection: "Are you filled?" This is because He promised that He would fill it with jinn and mankind, all of them. This is the apparent meaning of the context of the verse, and the hadiths point to it:

Al-Bukhari, commenting on this verse, said: Abdullah ibn Abi al-Aswad narrated to us, Harami ibn 'Umara narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "It is cast into the Fire, and it says: 'Is there any more?' until He places His foot in it, and it says: 'Qat, qat (enough, enough).'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4848.]

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Jahannam will continue to have people cast into it, and it will say: 'Is there any more?' until the Lord of Might places His foot in it, whereupon some of it draws in upon the other, and it says: 'Qat, qat, by Your might and Your generosity!' And Paradise will continue to have surplus, until Allah creates for it another creation, and He will settle them in the surplus of Paradise." [Al-Musnad, 3/234.]

Another hadith: Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Qattan narrated to us, Abu Sufyan al-Himyari Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Awf narrated to us, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, who raised it (to the Prophet), though Abu Sufyan mostly stopped it at Abu Hurayrah: "It is said to Jahannam: 'Are you filled?' and it says: 'Is there any more?' Then the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, places His foot upon it, and it says: 'Qat, qat.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4849.]

Another route: Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Paradise and the Fire disputed. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said to Paradise: 'You are My mercy; I show mercy through you to whomever I will of My servants.' And He said to the Fire: 'You are only My punishment; I punish through you whomever I will of My servants, and each of you will have its fill. As for the Fire, it will not be filled until He places His foot upon it, whereupon it says: "Qat, qat," and then it is filled, and some of it draws in upon the other, and Allah does not wrong any of His creation. As for Paradise, Allah will create for it another creation.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4850.]

Another hadith: Muslim said in his Sahih: Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Paradise and the Fire disputed. The Fire said: 'In me are the tyrants and the arrogant.' Paradise said: 'In me are the weak among people and their poor.' He judged between them, and said to Paradise: 'You are only My mercy; I show mercy through you to whomever I will of My servants.' And He said to the Fire: 'You are only My punishment; I punish through you whomever I will of My servants, and each of you will have its fill.'" Imam Ahmad narrated it by another route, from Abu Sa'id, with a fuller version, saying:

Hasan and Rawh narrated to us, both said: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Paradise and the Fire boasted. The Fire said: 'O Lord, there enter me the tyrants, the arrogant, the kings and the nobles.' Paradise said: 'O Lord, there enter me the weak, the poor and the needy.' Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says to the Fire: 'You are My punishment; I afflict with you whomever I will.' And He said to Paradise: 'You are My mercy, you encompass everything, and each of you will have its fill. Those of the Fire will be cast into it, and it says: "Is there any more?" He said: And it is cast into it, and it says: "Is there any more?" And it is cast into it, and it says: "Is there any more?" until its Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, comes to it and places His foot upon it, whereupon it draws in and says: "Enough, enough!" As for Paradise, it will remain with whatever Allah wills it to remain, and then Allah creates for it a creation as He wills.'" [Al-Musnad, 3/13.]

Then I will praise Him with a praise by which He will be pleased with me. Then I will be permitted to speak. Then my Ummah will pass over the Sirat, which is laid between the backs of Jahannam, and they will pass faster than the glance and the arrow, and faster than the best of horses, until a man comes out of it crawling, and those are their deeds. Jahannam will be asking for more, until He places His foot in it, whereupon some of it draws in upon the other and it says: 'Qat, qat!' And I will be at the Pool." It was said: "What is the Pool, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, its drink is whiter than milk, sweeter than honey, colder than snow, and its scent is better than musk. Its vessels are more numerous than the stars; whoever drinks from it will never thirst again, and it will never be withheld from anyone so that he is never satisfied." [Ibn Abi Asim in al-Sunnah, no. 790, by way of Uqbah ibn Mukram. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Yahya al-Hammani narrated to us, from Nadr al-Khazzaz, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿On the Day We say to Jahannam, "Are you filled?" and it says, "Is there any more?"﴾ He said: "It has not been filled." He said: "It says: 'Is there in me any place that can be added to me?'"

Similarly al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated from Ikrimah regarding ﴿and it says, "Is there any more?"﴾: "Is there in one place of entry, which has been filled?"

Al-Walid ibn Muslim said, from Yazid ibn Abi Maryam, that he heard Mujahid say: "It will continue to be thrown into it until it says: 'I am filled,' and it says: 'Is there any more in me?'" And from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, something similar.

Al-Awfi said, from Ibn Abbas: "That is when there is no place left in it that can hold even a needle." And Allah knows best.

* *

Imam Ahmad narrated it by another route, from Abu Sa'id, with a fuller version, saying:

Hasan and Rawh narrated to us, both said: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Paradise and the Fire boasted. The Fire said: 'O Lord, there enter me the tyrants, the arrogant, the kings and the nobles.' Paradise said: 'O Lord, there enter me the weak, the poor and the needy.' Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says to the Fire: 'You are My punishment; I afflict with you whomever I will.' And He said to Paradise: 'You are My mercy, you encompass everything, and each of you will have its fill. Those of the Fire will be cast into it, and it says: "Is there any more?" He said: And it is cast into it, and it says: "Is there any more?" And it is cast into it, and it says: "Is there any more?" until its Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, comes to it and places His foot upon it, whereupon it draws in and says: "Enough, enough!" As for Paradise, it will remain with whatever Allah wills it to remain, and then Allah creates for it a creation as He wills.'" [Al-Musnad, 3/13.]

Another hadith: Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said in his Musnad: Uqbah ibn Mukram narrated to us, Yunus narrated to us, Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from Udi ibn Thabit, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will make Himself known to me on the Day of Resurrection, and I will prostrate in a prostration by which He will be pleased with me. Then I will praise Him with a praise by which He will be pleased with me. Then I will be permitted to speak. Then my Ummah will pass over the Sirat, which is laid between the backs of Jahannam, and they will pass faster than the glance and the arrow, and faster than the best of horses, until a man comes out of it crawling, and those are their deeds. Jahannam will be asking for more, until He places His foot in it, whereupon some of it draws in upon the other and it says: 'Qat, qat!' And I will be at the Pool." It was said: "What is the Pool, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, its drink is whiter than milk, sweeter than honey, colder than snow, and its scent is better than musk. Its vessels are more numerous than the stars; whoever drinks from it will never thirst again, and it will never be withheld from anyone so that he is never satisfied." [Ibn Abi Asim in al-Sunnah, no. 790, by way of Uqbah ibn Mukram. Al-Albani said: "Its isnad is fabricated; its fault is Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim, Abu Maryam al-Ansari, who used to fabricate hadith, as said by Ibn al-Madini and Abu Dawud."] This view is the one chosen by Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Yahya al-Hammani narrated to us, from Nadr al-Khazzaz, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿On the Day We say to Jahannam, "Are you filled?" and it says, "Is there any more?"﴾ He said: "It has not been filled." He said: "It says: 'Is there in me any place that can be added to me?'"

Similarly al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated from Ikrimah regarding ﴿and it says, "Is there any more?"﴾: "Is there in one place of entry, which has been filled?"

Al-Walid ibn Muslim said, from Yazid ibn Abi Maryam, that he heard Mujahid say: "It will continue to be thrown into it until it says: 'I am filled,' and it says: 'Is there any more in me?'" And from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, something similar.

According to these scholars, the words of Allah, exalted is He, ﴿Are you filled?﴾ refer only to after He places His foot upon it, whereupon it draws in and says at that time: "Is there any remaining space in me that can hold anything?"

Al-Awfi said, from Ibn Abbas: "That is when there is no place left in it that can hold even a needle." And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous, not far away﴾: Qatadah, Abu Malik and al-Suddi said: ﴿brought near﴾ means it will be brought close and made nigh to the righteous, ﴿not far away﴾, and that is on the Day of Resurrection; it is not far, because it is certain to come, and everything that is to come is coming.

﴿This is what you were promised, for every constantly returning, watchful one﴾ [In A: "awwab hafiz"]: that is, one who returns repeatedly, repents, and desists. ﴿Watchful﴾: one who guards the covenant, so does not break or violate it.

Ubayd ibn Umayr said: "The awwab is the watchful one who does not sit in a gathering [and then rise] until he seeks forgiveness from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

﴿Who feared the Most Merciful unseen﴾: that is, who feared Allah in his secret, where no one sees him except Allah, as the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "And a man who remembers Allah in private, and his eyes overflow."

﴿And came with a heart turned in repentance﴾: that is, he meets Allah on the Day of Resurrection with a sound heart, turned in repentance to Him, humbled before Him.

﴿Enter it in peace﴾: that is, Paradise. Qatadah said: "They are safe from the punishment of Allah, and the angels of Allah greet them."

* *

As for His words: ﴿That is the Day of Eternity﴾: that is, they will abide forever in Paradise; they will never die, never leave, and never seek to be moved from it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿For them is whatever they will therein﴾: that is, whatever kind of pleasures they choose and seek, it will be brought to them.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Amr ibn Uthman narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, from Bahir ibn Sa'd, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Kathir ibn Murrah, who said: "Among the increase [al-mazid] is that a cloud passes over the people of Paradise and says: 'What do you want, that I may rain it down for you?' They do not ask for anything except that it rains it upon them." Kuthayyir said: "If Allah makes me witness that, I will surely say: 'Rain upon us, O maidens adorned.'"

And in a hadith from Ibn Mas'ud, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Indeed you will desire birds in Paradise, and one will fall before you roasted." [Narrated by al-Hasan ibn Arafah in his Juz' (22), al-Bazzar in his Musnad (3532, Kashf al-Astar), and Ibn Adi in al-Kamil (6/689), by way of Khalaf ibn Khalifah, from Humayd al-A'raj, from Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn Mas'ud, raised. In its isnad is Humayd al-A'raj; al-Bukhari said: "munkar al-hadith," and Ibn Hibban said: "his hadiths resemble fabrications."]

Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Amir al-Ahwal, from Abu al-Siddiq [in M: "from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq"], from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If the believer desires a child in Paradise, its pregnancy, birth and growing up will happen in a single hour."

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, from Bundar, from Mu'adh ibn Hisham, with the same. [Al-Musnad (3/9); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2563; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 4338.] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib," and he added "as he desires."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And with Us is more﴾: like His words, exalted is He: ﴿For those who did good is the best reward and more﴾ [Yunus: 26]. It has already been mentioned in Sahih Muslim, from Suhayb ibn Sinan al-Rumi, that it is the looking upon the Noble Face of Allah. Al-Bazzar and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated, from the hadith of Sharik al-Qadi, from Uthman ibn Umayr Abu al-Yaqzan, from Anas ibn Malik, regarding the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And with Us is more﴾: He said: "The Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, will manifest Himself to them every Friday."

Al-Imam Abu Abdullah al-Shafi'i also narrated it as a marfu' hadith, saying in his Musnad: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad informed us; Musa ibn Ubayda narrated to me; Abu al-Azhar Mu'awiyah ibn Ishaq ibn Talha narrated to me, from Abd Allah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr [In M: "from Ubayd Allah ibn Umayr", while in the original: "Abd Allah Umayr"; the correction is from al-Shafi'i's al-Umm.] that he heard Anas ibn Malik say: Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah with a white mirror in which there was a spot, and the Prophet [In M: "Messenger of Allah".] ﷺ said: "What is this?" He said: "This is Friday, which you and your community have been favoured with. The people are followers of you in it: the Jews and the Christians. And for you in it is goodness, and for you in it is an hour in which no believing servant meets it while calling upon Allah for some good except that it is answered for him, and it is, with us, the Day of Increase (Yawm al-Mazid)." The Prophet ﷺ said: "O Jibril, and what is the Day of Increase?" He said: "Your Lord has taken in al-Firdaws a wide valley in which there are mounds of musk. When it is the day of Friday, Allah sends down whomever He wills [In M: "people".] of His angels, and around Him are pulpits of light, upon which are the seats of the Prophets, and those pulpits are surrounded by pulpits of gold, adorned with rubies and chrysolite, upon which are the martyrs and the truthful [In A: "the righteous".], and they sit behind them upon those mounds. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am your Lord, I have fulfilled My promise to you, so ask Me and I will give you.' They say: 'Our Lord, we ask You for Your pleasure.' He says: 'I am pleased with you, and for you is what you have wished for, and with Me is increase.' So they love Friday because of the good their Lord gives them in it, and it is the day on which your Lord settled upon the Throne, and in it Adam was created, and in it the Hour will be established."

Thus al-Imam al-Shafi'i narrated it in the chapter "al-Jumu'ah" of al-Umm [al-Umm (1/185).], and it has chains from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him. Ibn Jarir also reported this from the narration of Uthman ibn Umayr, from Anas, in a fuller form than this [Tafsir al-Tabari (26/109).]. He also mentioned here a lengthy report from Anas ibn Malik as a mawquf narration, and in it are many strange (gharib) elements [Tafsir al-Tabari (26/109).].

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us; Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us; Darraj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Indeed a man in Paradise will recline in Paradise for seventy years before he moves. Then a woman will come to him and strike his shoulder, and he will look at his face in her cheek, clearer than a mirror. And indeed the smallest pearl upon her illuminates what is between the East and the West. She will greet him, and he will return the greeting, and he will ask her: 'Who are you?' She will say: 'I am of the Mazid.' Upon her are seventy garments, the least of which is like al-Nu'man of Tuba, and his sight will penetrate them until he sees the marrow of her shin from behind all that. And upon her are crowns; indeed the smallest pearl among them illuminates what is between the East and the West." [Al-Musnad (3/75), in which: Darraj from Abu al-Haytham, weak (da'if).]

Likewise, Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated it from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Darraj, with the same [Reported by al-Tabari in his tafsir (26/110), and the discussion on it is like the preceding.].

Ibn Kathir says that Allah, exalted is He, tells Hell on the Day of Resurrection: "Are you filled?" This is because He promised that He would fill it with jinn and mankind, all of them. He, glory be to Him, commands whoever He commands to be cast into it, and it is thrown in while it says: ﴿Is there any more?﴾ That is, "Is there anything left that you can add to me?" This is the apparent meaning of the context of the verse, and the hadiths point to it:

Al-Bukhari, commenting on this verse, said: Abdullah ibn Abi al-Aswad narrated to us, Harami ibn 'Umara narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "It is cast into the Fire, and it says: 'Is there any more?' until He places His foot in it, and it says: 'Qat, qat (enough, enough).'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4848.]

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Jahannam will continue to have people cast into it, and it will say: 'Is there any more?' until the Lord of Might places His foot in it, whereupon some of it draws in upon the other, and it says: 'Qat, qat, by Your might and Your generosity!' And Paradise will continue to have surplus, until Allah creates for it another creation, and He will settle them in the surplus of Paradise." [Al-Musnad, 3/234.]

Then Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Qatadah, in similar wording. [Sahih Muslim, no. 4848.] And Aban al-Attar and Sulayman al-Taymi narrated it from Qatadah, in similar wording. [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir, 26/106.]

Another hadith: Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Qattan narrated to us, Abu Sufyan al-Himyari Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Awf narrated to us, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, who raised it (to the Prophet), though Abu Sufyan mostly stopped it at Abu Hurayrah: "It is said to Jahannam: 'Are you filled?' and it says: 'Is there any more?' Then the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, places His foot upon it, and it says: 'Qat, qat.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4849.]

It was narrated by Ayyub and Hisham ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, with the same. [Ahmad in his Musnad (2/507) by way of Hisham ibn Hassan; al-Tabari in his Tafsir (26/107) by way of Ayyub and Hisham ibn Hassan.]

Another route: Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Paradise and the Fire disputed. The Fire said: 'I have been given the arrogant and the haughty.' Paradise said: 'What is it with me that only the weak among people and their lowly enter me?' Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said to Paradise: 'You are My mercy; I show mercy through you to whomever I will of My servants.' And He said to the Fire: 'You are only My punishment; I punish through you whomever I will of My servants, and each of you will have its fill. As for the Fire, it will not be filled until He places His foot upon it, whereupon it says: "Qat, qat," and then it is filled, and some of it draws in upon the other, and Allah does not wrong any of His creation. As for Paradise, Allah will create for it another creation.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4850.]

Another hadith: Muslim said in his Sahih: Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Paradise and the Fire disputed. The Fire said: 'In me are the tyrants and the arrogant.' Paradise said: 'In me are the weak among people and their poor.' He judged between them, and said to Paradise: 'You are only My mercy; I show mercy through you to whomever I will of My servants.' And He said to the Fire: 'You are only My punishment; I punish through you whomever I will of My servants, and each of you will have its fill.'" Muslim alone narrated it by this route, not al-Bukhari. [Sahih Muslim, no. 2847.] And Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad narrated it by another route, from Abu Sa'id, with a fuller version, saying:

Hasan and Rawh narrated to us, both said: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Paradise and the Fire boasted. He said: And it is cast into it, and it says: "Is there any more?" And it is cast into it, and it says: "Is there any more?" until its Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, comes to it and places His foot upon it, whereupon it draws in and says: "Enough, enough!" Another hadith: Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said in his Musnad: Uqbah ibn Mukram narrated to us, Yunus narrated to us, Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from Udi ibn Thabit, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will make Himself known to me on the Day of Resurrection, and I will prostrate in a prostration by which He will be pleased with me. And upon her are crowns; indeed the smallest pearl among them illuminates what is between the East and the West." [Al-Musnad (3/75), in which: Darraj from Abu al-Haytham, weak (da'if).]

Likewise, Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated it from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Darraj, with the same [Reported by al-Tabari in his tafsir (26/110), and the discussion on it is like the preceding.].

Ibn Kathir says that Allah, exalted is He, tells Hell on the Day of Resurrection: "Are you filled?" This is because He promised that He would fill it with jinn and mankind, all of them. He, glory be to Him, commands whoever He commands to be cast into it, and it is thrown in while it says: ﴿Is there any more?﴾ That is, "Is there anything left that you can add to me?" This is the apparent meaning of the context of the verse, and the hadiths point to it:

Al-Bukhari, commenting on this verse, said: Abdullah ibn Abi al-Aswad narrated to us, Harami ibn 'Umara narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "It is cast into the Fire, and it says: 'Is there any more?' until He places His foot in it, and it says: 'Qat, qat (enough, enough).'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4848.]

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Jahannam will continue to have people cast into it, and it will say: 'Is there any more?' until the Lord of Might places His foot in it, whereupon some of it draws in upon the other, and it says: 'Qat, qat, by Your might and Your generosity!' And Paradise will continue to have surplus, until Allah creates for it another creation, and He will settle them in the surplus of Paradise." [Al-Musnad, 3/234.]

Then Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Qatadah, in similar wording. [Sahih Muslim, no. 4848.] And Aban al-Attar and Sulayman al-Taymi narrated it from Qatadah, in similar wording. [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir, 26/106.]

Another hadith: Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Qattan narrated to us, Abu Sufyan al-Himyari Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Awf narrated to us, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, who raised it (to the Prophet), though Abu Sufyan mostly stopped it at Abu Hurayrah: "It is said to Jahannam: 'Are you filled?' and it says: 'Is there any more?' Then the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, places His foot upon it, and it says: 'Qat, qat.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4849.]

It was narrated by Ayyub and Hisham ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, with the same. [Ahmad in his Musnad (2/507) by way of Hisham ibn Hassan; al-Tabari in his Tafsir (26/107) by way of Ayyub and Hisham ibn Hassan.]

Another route: Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Paradise and the Fire disputed. The Fire said: 'I have been given the arrogant and the haughty.' Paradise said: 'What is it with me that only the weak among people and their lowly enter me?' Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said to Paradise: 'You are My mercy; I show mercy through you to whomever I will of My servants.' And He said to the Fire: 'You are only My punishment; I punish through you whomever I will of My servants, and each of you will have its fill. As for the Fire, it will not be filled until He places His foot upon it, whereupon it says: "Qat, qat," and then it is filled, and some of it draws in upon the other, and Allah does not wrong any of His creation. As for Paradise, Allah will create for it another creation.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4850.]

Another hadith: Muslim said in his Sahih: Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Paradise and the Fire disputed. The Fire said: 'In me are the tyrants and the arrogant.' Paradise said: 'In me are the weak among people and their poor.' He judged between them, and said to Paradise: 'You are only My mercy; I show mercy through you to whomever I will of My servants.' And He said to the Fire: 'You are only My punishment; I punish through you whomever I will of My servants, and each of you will have its fill.'" Muslim alone narrated it by this route, not al-Bukhari. [Sahih Muslim, no. 2847.] And Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad narrated it by another route, from Abu Sa'id, with a fuller version, saying:

Hasan and Rawh narrated to us, both said: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Paradise and the Fire boasted. The Fire said: 'O Lord, there enter me the tyrants, the arrogant, the kings and the nobles.' Paradise said: 'O Lord, there enter me the weak, the poor and the needy.' Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says to the Fire: 'You are My punishment; I afflict with you whomever I will.' And He said to Paradise: 'You are My mercy, you encompass everything, and each of you will have its fill. Those of the Fire will be cast into it, and it says: "Is there any more?" He said: And it is cast into it, and it says: "Is there any more?" And it is cast into it, and it says: "Is there any more?" until its Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, comes to it and places His foot upon it, whereupon it draws in and says: "Enough, enough!" As for Paradise, it will remain with whatever Allah wills it to remain, and then Allah creates for it a creation as He wills.'" [Al-Musnad, 3/13.]

Another hadith: Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said in his Musnad: Uqbah ibn Mukram narrated to us, Yunus narrated to us, Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from Udi ibn Thabit, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will make Himself known to me on the Day of Resurrection, and I will prostrate in a prostration by which He will be pleased with me. Then I will praise Him with a praise by which He will be pleased with me. Then I will be permitted to speak. Then my Ummah will pass over the Sirat, which is laid between the backs of Jahannam, and they will pass faster than the glance and the arrow, and faster than the best of horses, until a man comes out of it crawling, and those are their deeds. Jahannam will be asking for more, until He places His foot in it, whereupon some of it draws in upon the other and it says: 'Qat, qat!' And I will be at the Pool." It was said: "What is the Pool, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, its drink is whiter than milk, sweeter than honey, colder than snow, and its scent is better than musk. Its vessels are more numerous than the stars; whoever drinks from it will never thirst again, and it will never be withheld from anyone so that he is never satisfied." [Ibn Abi Asim in al-Sunnah, no. 790, by way of Uqbah ibn Mukram. Al-Albani said: "Its isnad is fabricated; its fault is Abd al-Ghaffar ibn al-Qasim, Abu Maryam al-Ansari, who used to fabricate hadith, as said by Ibn al-Madini and Abu Dawud."] This view is the one chosen by Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Yahya al-Hammani narrated to us, from Nadr al-Khazzaz, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿On the Day We say to Jahannam, "Are you filled?" and it says, "Is there any more?"﴾ He said: "It has not been filled." He said: "It says: 'Is there in me any place that can be added to me?'"

Similarly al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated from Ikrimah regarding ﴿and it says, "Is there any more?"﴾: "Is there in one place of entry, which has been filled?"

Al-Walid ibn Muslim said, from Yazid ibn Abi Maryam, that he heard Mujahid say: "It will continue to be thrown into it until it says: 'I am filled,' and it says: 'Is there any more in me?'" And from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, something similar.

According to these scholars, the words of Allah, exalted is He, ﴿Are you filled?﴾ refer only to after He places His foot upon it, whereupon it draws in and says at that time: "Is there any remaining space in me that can hold anything?"

Al-Awfi said, from Ibn Abbas: "That is when there is no place left in it that can hold even a needle." And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous, not far away﴾: Qatadah, Abu Malik and al-Suddi said: ﴿brought near﴾ means it will be brought close and made nigh to the righteous, ﴿not far away﴾, and that is on the Day of Resurrection; it is not far, because it is certain to come, and everything that is to come is coming.

﴿This is what you were promised, for every constantly returning, watchful one﴾ [In A: "awwab hafiz"]: that is, one who returns repeatedly, repents, and desists. ﴿Watchful﴾: one who guards the covenant, so does not break or violate it.

Ubayd ibn Umayr said: "The awwab is the watchful one who does not sit in a gathering [and then rise] until he seeks forgiveness from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

﴿Who feared the Most Merciful unseen﴾: that is, who feared Allah in his secret, where no one sees him except Allah, as the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "And a man who remembers Allah in private, and his eyes overflow."

﴿And came with a heart turned in repentance﴾: that is, he meets Allah on the Day of Resurrection with a sound heart, turned in repentance to Him, humbled before Him.

﴿Enter it in peace﴾: that is, Paradise. Qatadah said: "They are safe from the punishment of Allah, and the angels of Allah greet them."

* *

As for His words: ﴿That is the Day of Eternity﴾: that is, they will abide forever in Paradise; they will never die, never leave, and never seek to be moved from it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿For them is whatever they will therein﴾: that is, whatever kind of pleasures they choose and seek, it will be brought to them.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Amr ibn Uthman narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, from Bahir ibn Sa'd, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Kathir ibn Murrah, who said: "Among the increase [al-mazid] is that a cloud passes over the people of Paradise and says: 'What do you want, that I may rain it down for you?' They do not ask for anything except that it rains it upon them." Kuthayyir said: "If Allah makes me witness that, I will surely say: 'Rain upon us, O maidens adorned.'"

And in a hadith from Ibn Mas'ud, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Indeed you will desire birds in Paradise, and one will fall before you roasted." [Narrated by al-Hasan ibn Arafah in his Juz' (22), al-Bazzar in his Musnad (3532, Kashf al-Astar), and Ibn Adi in al-Kamil (6/689), by way of Khalaf ibn Khalifah, from Humayd al-A'raj, from Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn Mas'ud, raised. In its isnad is Humayd al-A'raj; al-Bukhari said: "munkar al-hadith," and Ibn Hibban said: "his hadiths resemble fabrications."]

Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Amir al-Ahwal, from Abu al-Siddiq [in M: "from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq"], from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If the believer desires a child in Paradise, its pregnancy, birth and growing up will happen in a single hour."

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, from Bundar, from Mu'adh ibn Hisham, with the same. [Al-Musnad (3/9); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2563; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 4338.] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib," and he added "as he desires."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And with Us is more﴾: like His words, exalted is He: ﴿For those who did good is the best reward and more﴾ [Yunus: 26]. It has already been mentioned in Sahih Muslim, from Suhayb ibn Sinan al-Rumi, that it is the looking upon the Noble Face of Allah. Al-Bazzar and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated, from the hadith of Sharik al-Qadi, from Uthman ibn Umayr Abu al-Yaqzan, from Anas ibn Malik, regarding the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And with Us is more﴾: He said: "The Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, will manifest Himself to them every Friday."

Al-Imam Abu Abdullah al-Shafi'i also narrated it as a marfu' hadith, saying in his Musnad: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad informed us; Musa ibn Ubayda narrated to me; Abu al-Azhar Mu'awiyah ibn Ishaq ibn Talha narrated to me, from Abd Allah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr [In M: "from Ubayd Allah ibn Umayr", while in the original: "Abd Allah Umayr"; the correction is from al-Shafi'i's al-Umm.] that he heard Anas ibn Malik say: Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah with a white mirror in which there was a spot, and the Prophet [In M: "Messenger of Allah".] ﷺ said: "What is this?" He said: "This is Friday, which you and your community have been favoured with. The people are followers of you in it: the Jews and the Christians. And for you in it is goodness, and for you in it is an hour in which no believing servant meets it while calling upon Allah for some good except that it is answered for him, and it is, with us, the Day of Increase (Yawm al-Mazid)." The Prophet ﷺ said: "O Jibril, and what is the Day of Increase?" He said: "Your Lord has taken in al-Firdaws a wide valley in which there are mounds of musk. When it is the day of Friday, Allah sends down whomever He wills [In M: "people".] of His angels, and around Him are pulpits of light, upon which are the seats of the Prophets, and those pulpits are surrounded by pulpits of gold, adorned with rubies and chrysolite, upon which are the martyrs and the truthful [In A: "the righteous".], and they sit behind them upon those mounds. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am your Lord, I have fulfilled My promise to you, so ask Me and I will give you.' They say: 'Our Lord, we ask You for Your pleasure.' He says: 'I am pleased with you, and for you is what you have wished for, and with Me is increase.' So they love Friday because of the good their Lord gives them in it, and it is the day on which your Lord settled upon the Throne, and in it Adam was created, and in it the Hour will be established."

Thus al-Imam al-Shafi'i narrated it in the chapter "al-Jumu'ah" of al-Umm [al-Umm (1/185).], and it has chains from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him. Ibn Jarir also reported this from the narration of Uthman ibn Umayr, from Anas, in a fuller form than this [Tafsir al-Tabari (26/109).]. He also mentioned here a lengthy report from Anas ibn Malik as a mawquf narration, and in it are many strange (gharib) elements [Tafsir al-Tabari (26/109).].

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us; Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us; Darraj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Indeed a man in Paradise will recline in Paradise for seventy years before he moves. Then a woman will come to him and strike his shoulder, and he will look at his face in her cheek, clearer than a mirror. And indeed the smallest pearl upon her illuminates what is between the East and the West. She will greet him, and he will return the greeting, and he will ask her: 'Who are you?' She will say: 'I am of the Mazid.' Upon her are seventy garments, the least of which is like al-Nu'man of Tuba, and his sight will penetrate them until he sees the marrow of her shin from behind all that. And upon her are crowns; indeed the smallest pearl among them illuminates what is between the East and the West." [Al-Musnad (3/75), in which: Darraj from Abu al-Haytham, weak (da'if).]

Likewise, Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated it from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Darraj, with the same [Reported by al-Tabari in his tafsir (26/110), and the discussion on it is like the preceding.].

**Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 50, verses 36–40:**

Allah, the Exalted, says: "And how many generations did We destroy before these deniers" [[In M and A: "the deniers" (al-mukadhdhibin).]] "who were mightier than them in strength." That is, they were greater in number and stronger in might, and they tilled the earth and cultivated it more than these people did. Therefore He says here: "and they roamed through the lands." Ibn Abbas said: "They left their mark upon it." Mujahid said regarding "and they roamed through the lands": "They traveled across the earth." Qatadah said: "They journeyed through the lands," meaning they traveled through them seeking provision, trade and gain, more than you have traveled through them. It is said of one who wanders through the lands: "naqqaba fiha" (he roamed in them). Imru' al-Qays said:

"I have roamed the horizons until
I was content with gain and with return."

[[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (26/110).]]

His words: "Is there any escape?" mean: Was there any way to flee from the decree and destiny of Allah? Did what they gathered benefit them, or did it avert the punishment of Allah when it came upon them, after they denied the Messengers? So you too have no escape, no refuge, no way out, and no means of evasion.

* *

His words: "Indeed in that is a reminder" mean: indeed in that is a lesson, "for whoever has a heart," meaning a mind with which he understands. Mujahid said: "that is, intellect." "Or gives ear while he is present" means: he listens to the speech and takes it in, comprehends it with his heart and grasps it with his mind.

Mujahid also said regarding "or gives ear": that is, he does not occupy his soul with anything else. "And he is present" — he said: "present with the heart."

Ad-Dahhak said: The Arabs say, "So-and-so gave his ear" when he listens with his two ears while being present, saying "not absent." Al-Thawri and others said the same.

* *

His words: "And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no weariness touched Us." In this is an affirmation of the Return, for whoever is able to create the heavens and the earth and is not tired by their creation is even more surely able to bring the dead back to life.

Qatadah said: The Jews — may the curses of Allah be upon them — said: "Allah created the heavens and the earth in six days, then rested on the seventh day, which is Saturday; they call it the Day of Rest." So Allah revealed His refutation of what they said and interpreted: "and no weariness touched Us," meaning no exhaustion, no fatigue, and no toil. As He says in another verse: "Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and was not wearied by their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, indeed He is over all things competent" [46:33]; and as He says: "The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind" [40:57]; and He says: "Are you more difficult to create, or is the sky which He constructed?" [79:27].

* *

His words: "So be patient over what they say" — meaning the deniers. Be patient with them and "leave them with gracious avoidance" [73:10]. "And glorify your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting." The obligatory prayer before the Night Journey (al-Isra') consisted of two prayers: one before sunrise, at the time of Fajr, and one before sunset, at the time of 'Asr. Night prayer (qiyam al-layl) was obligatory upon the Prophet ﷺ and upon his Ummah for a year; then its obligation was abrogated (naskh) for his Ummah. Then, afterward, Allah abrogated all of that on the night of the Night Journey, replacing it with five prayers. Among them, however, are the Subh (Fajr) prayer and the 'Asr prayer, which are "before the rising of the sun and before the setting."

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Jarir ibn Abdullah, who said: "We were sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said: 'Indeed you will be presented to your Lord, and you will see Him as you see this moon; you will not be harmed in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in a prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do it.'" Then he recited: "And glorify your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before the setting."

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and the rest of the compilers narrated it through the chain of Isma'il, with the same wording. [[Al-Musnad (4/365); Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4851); Sahih Muslim no. (633); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3729); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2551); al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11330); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (117).]]

* *

His words: "And during part of the night glorify Him" mean: pray to Him during it, as in His words: "And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional [prayer] for you; it may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station" [17:79].

"And after the prostrations" — Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: it is the glorification after the prayer.

This is supported by what is established in the two Sahihs from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The poor among the Emigrants came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the people of wealth have taken the high ranks and everlasting bliss." He said: "And what is that?" They said: "They pray as we pray, they fast as we fast, they give charity and we do not give charity, and they free slaves and we do not free slaves!" He said: "Shall I not teach you something which, if you do it, you will surpass those after you, and no one will be better than you except one who does the same as you? Glorify (Subhan Allah), praise (Alhamdulillah) and magnify (Allahu akbar) thirty-three times after every prayer." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, our brothers, the people of wealth, have heard what we have done, and they have done the same." He said: "That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6329); Sahih Muslim no. (595).]]

The second opinion: the meaning of His words "and after the prostrations" is the two rak'ahs after Maghrib. This was narrated from Umar, Ali, his son al-Hasan, Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurayrah, and Abu Umamah, and this is the view of Mujahid, Ikrimah, al-Sha'bi, al-Nakha'i, al-Hasan, Qatadah and others.

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' and 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Asim ibn Damrah, from Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray two rak'ahs after every obligatory prayer, except Fajr and 'Asr. 'Abd al-Rahman said: "after every prayer."

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, with the same chain. [[Al-Musnad (1/124); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1275); al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (341).]] Al-Nasa'i added: "and Mutarrif, from Abu Ishaq, with the same." [[Al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (346).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamdani narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Rishdin ibn Kurayb, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "I spent a night with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he prayed two light rak'ahs, the two before Fajr. Then he went out to the prayer and said: 'O Ibn Abbas, two rak'ahs before the Fajr prayer are [at] the retreat of the stars, and two rak'ahs after Maghrib are [at] the retreat of the prostrations.'"

It was narrated by al-Tirmidhi from Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i, from Muhammad ibn Fudayl, with the same. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3275).]] He said: "Gharib (unusual); we do not know it except from this route."

The hadith of Ibn Abbas, that he spent the night in the house of his maternal aunt Maymunah and prayed with the Prophet ﷺ thirteen rak'ahs that night, is established in the two Sahihs [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1198); Sahih Muslim no. (763).]] and elsewhere. As for this addition, it is gharib and is not known except through this route. Rishdin ibn Kurayb is weak, and it may well be a statement of Ibn Abbas himself, halted at him (mawquf). And Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' and 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Asim ibn Damrah, from Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray two rak'ahs after every obligatory prayer, except Fajr and 'Asr. 'Abd al-Rahman said: "after every prayer."

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, with the same chain. [[Al-Musnad (1/124); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1275); al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (341).]] Al-Nasa'i added: "and Mutarrif, from Abu Ishaq, with the same." [[Al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (346).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamdani narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Rishdin ibn Kurayb, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "I spent a night with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he prayed two light rak'ahs, the two before Fajr. Then he went out to the prayer and said: 'O Ibn Abbas, two rak'ahs before the Fajr prayer are [at] the retreat of the stars, and two rak'ahs after Maghrib are [at] the retreat of the prostrations.'"

(1198); Sahih Muslim no. (763).]] and elsewhere. As for this addition, it is gharib and is not known except through this route. **Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 50, verses 41–45:**

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And listen⦆, O Muhammad, ﴿on the day when the caller calls from a near place⦆. Qatadah said: Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Allah commands an angel [[Variant from manuscript M: "angels".]] [[Addition from manuscript M.]] to call out from the rock of Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem): "O decayed bones and scattered joints, indeed Allah commands you to gather for the decision of judgement."

﴿On the day they hear the Cry in truth⦆, meaning the blast of the Trumpet, which comes with the truth about which most of them were in doubt. ﴿That is the Day of Coming Forth⦆, that is, from the graves.

﴿Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and to Us is the final return⦆. That is, it is He who originates creation and then restores it, and that is easier for Him. To Him is the return of all creatures, and He will recompense each one for their deeds: if good, then good; if evil, then evil.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿On the day when the earth splits asunder from them, swiftly⦆: this is because Allah, the Exalted, sends down rain from the sky, by which the bodies of creatures grow in their graves, just as seeds grow in moist earth through water. When the bodies are complete, Allah commands Israfil, and he blows into the Trumpet. The souls have been placed in an opening in the Trumpet, and when Israfil blows into it, the souls come out, blazing between the heaven and the earth. Allah, the Exalted, says: "By My might and My majesty, every soul will surely return to the body which it used to inhabit." Every soul then returns to its body, and it spreads through it as poison spreads through one who has been stung. The earth splits open from them, and they rise swiftly to the place of reckoning, hastening to the command of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿hastening toward the caller; the disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult day."⦆ [Al-Qamar: 8]. Allah, the Exalted, also says: ﴿The day He calls you, and you will respond with His praise, and you will think that you remained only a little.⦆ [Al-Isra: 52]

In Sahih Muslim, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I will be the first one from whom the earth is split open." [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. 2278, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him). I did not find it from the hadith of Anas.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿That is a gathering that is easy for Us⦆: that is, that re-creation is easy for Us and simple in Our sight, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye⦆ [Al-Qamar: 50]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Your creation and your resurrection are but as a single soul. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing⦆ [Luqman: 28].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿We know best what they say⦆: that is, Our knowledge encompasses what the polytheists say to you of denial, so let that not distress you. This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We certainly know that your breast is constricted by what they say. So glorify your Lord with praise and be among those who prostrate. And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty.⦆ [Al-Hijr: 97–99]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And you are not over them a compeller⦆: that is, you are not one who forces these people to guidance, and that is not what you were charged with.

Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: ﴿And you are not over them a compeller⦆ means: you should not act tyrannically toward them.

The first opinion is more correct. Had He intended what they said, He would have said, "And do not be a tyrant over them." Rather, He said ﴿And you are not over them a compeller⦆, meaning: you are not one who compels them to faith; you are only a conveyor of the message.

Al-Farra' said: I heard the Arabs say: "So-and-so compelled so-and-so to such-and-such," meaning he forced him to it. [[In manuscript M: "Jabara fulan 'ala fulan kadhā".]] [[See Tafsir al-Tabari (26/115).]]

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So remind, by the Qur'an, whoever fears My warning⦆: that is, you deliver the message of your Lord, for only one who fears Allah and His warning and hopes for His promise will be reminded, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Your duty is only to deliver, and upon Us is the reckoning⦆ [Al-Ra'd: 40], and His saying: ﴿So remind; you are only a reminder. For this reason He said here: ﴿And you are not over them a compeller. So remind, by the Qur'an, whoever fears My warning⦆.

Qatadah used to say: "O Allah, make us among those who fear Your warning and hope for Your promise, O Most Kind, O Most Merciful."

The end of the tafsir of Surah Qaf. All praise is for Allah alone, and Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs.

Qatadah used to say: "O Allah, make us among those who fear Your warning and hope for Your promise, O Most Kind, O Most Merciful."

The end of the tafsir of Surah Qaf. All praise is for Allah alone, and Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs.
